# Relay

# Talk to your agents from your phone.

> Build agents people can message.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/index.md

## Start here

Connect your coding agent in three steps: install Relay, connect it, send it a message from your phone. Your agent runs on your computer or your backend. You message it in Relay, and it replies in the same chat.

<CardGroup cols={2}>
  <Card title="Connect your coding agent" href="#connect-your-coding-agent" icon="terminal">Give the coding agent you already use a place to receive messages.</Card>
  <Card title="Build on the API" href="#or-build-on-the-api" icon="code">Send messages from your own backend with an Agent Token.</Card>
</CardGroup>


## What you need

Install Relay on your phone from [relayapp.im](https://relayapp.im). Have a coding agent installed on your computer, and Node.js 22.22.3 or newer. Keep your computer and the agent running while you message it. Check your Node.js version with this command:

```bash
node --version
```

The coding-agent path creates an agent and saves its token privately on your computer. If you build on the API instead, get an [Agent Token](/live/authentication) first.


## Connect your coding agent

Run the connect command for the product you use. Replace `claude-code` with `codex`, `cursor`, `opencode`, `cline`, `vscode`, `gemini-cli`, `claude-desktop`, `hermes`, or `openclaw`. Relay creates a new agent, saves its token privately on this computer, and adds itself to the product's configuration. It prints the plan and asks before it changes anything.

```bash
npx relaymessenger@staging connect claude-code
```

Add `--dry-run` to read the plan without applying it. When connect finishes, open or restart the product as the plan directs. Each product's page under [Integrations](/integrations/claude-code) lists its startup steps and what it supports.


## Message it from your phone

Watch the agent's chat from your terminal while you send the first message. Replace `YOUR_AGENT_HANDLE` with the handle connect printed. The view prints a QR code and a share link; open the link on your phone, or scan the code, and send `hello` in Relay.

```bash
npx relaymessenger@staging watch YOUR_AGENT_HANDLE
```

The watch view only observes. Your coding agent must stay running to receive the message and reply. Press `q` or `Ctrl-C` to stop watching; the agent keeps running.

<Frame caption="Your message and the agent's reply in Relay.">
<img alt="Relay phone chat showing a sent message and an agent reply" width="184" height="400" src="data:image/png;base64," />
</Frame>


## Or build on the API

Send and read messages from your own backend with an Agent Token, in TypeScript or with cURL. [Build on the API](/start/build-on-the-api) walks through the SDK setup, the first send, a follow-up, and reading history.

## Group chats and mentions

A group chat holds one person and up to six agents. Mention an agent by handle when you address it: send the text with `POST /v1/chats/{chatId}/messages`, set `mention` to the agent's handle, and set `mention_range` to the position of its name in the text. The range counts UTF-16 units, so most characters count as 1 and some emoji count as 2. Text parts in returned messages carry a `mentions` array with `id`, `handle`, `is_me`, and `range`, or `mentions: null` when nothing is mentioned. Store ids, not handles, because a handle can change. Branch on `is_me` to learn whether the mention addresses your agent. [Mentions](/concepts/messages/mentions) shows a full request and its response, and [Group chats](/concepts/chats/group-chats) covers the recipient rules.

## Receive events

Give Relay an HTTPS endpoint for `message.received` events: create a subscription with `POST /v1/webhook-subscriptions`, passing your `target_url` and the `subscribed_events` you want. Relay sends every event to that address as an HTTP POST with a signed body. The response carries the subscription and its `signing_secret`. Relay returns the secret only in this response, so save it as `RELAY_WEBHOOK_SECRET` now; every later request for the subscription omits it. [Create a subscription](/events/webhooks/subscriptions) walks through the request, and [the reference](/api-reference/webhooks/create-a-new-webhook-subscription) lists every field.

Verify the raw body before you parse it. Write each verified event to your own store once, then acknowledge it. Relay waits ten seconds for your response and retries when it gets none, so do slow work after the write, not before. In this receiver `acceptOnce` is your durable inbox operation, not an SDK method:

```typescript
import Relay, { type RelayWebhookEvent } from "@relaymessenger/sdk";

const receiver = new Relay({
  apiKey: process.env.RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN!,
  baseURL: "https://api.staging.relayapp.im",
  webhookSecret: process.env.RELAY_WEBHOOK_SECRET!,
});

export async function receive(
  request: Request,
  acceptOnce: (event: RelayWebhookEvent) => Promise<void>,
): Promise<Response> {
  let event: RelayWebhookEvent;
  try {
    event = receiver.webhooks.unwrap(await request.text(), {
      headers: request.headers,
    });
  } catch {
    return new Response("Webhook rejected", { status: 401 });
  }
  try {
    await acceptOnce(event);
  } catch {
    return new Response("Inbox unavailable", { status: 503 });
  }
  return new Response(null, { status: 204 });
}
```

Continue with [webhook verification](/events/webhooks) for the signature rules, or [WebSocket events](/events/websocket/observe-events) if your agent cannot expose an HTTPS endpoint.

## Your agent’s identity

Every agent has a name, an About line, a picture, a handle, a share link, and a QR code. The default About is `A Relay agent, created with relay agents create.` The default picture is a bird tile chosen by the handle. Read your agent's own card with this request:

<CodeGroup>
```bash cURL
curl -sS -A "relay-docs/1.0" \
  "https://api.staging.relayapp.im/v1/contact_card?handle=relay_staging_fullsync" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN"
```

```typescript TypeScript SDK
const card = await relay.contactCard.retrieve({
  handle: "relay_staging_fullsync",
});
console.log(card);
```
</CodeGroup>

The response lists the matching cards. This agent was created before the bird default, so its `image_url` is `null`; a new agent gets a picture address here.

```json captured-output
{
  "contact_cards": [
    {
      "handle": "relay_staging_fullsync",
      "kind": "agent",
      "first_name": "Staging Full Sync",
      "last_name": null,
      "image_url": null,
      "is_active": true
    }
  ]
}
```

Change the name in [Contact Card settings](/concepts/identity/contact-card), the picture in [profile photos](/concepts/identity/profile-photos), and read the share link and QR code from the CLI watch view.

## Going live

Handle errors by code, keep the trace ID for support, and reuse the message's idempotency key on every retry of the same message. A rate limit returns HTTP 429 with error code `2008` and a `retry_after` value in seconds; wait that long, then retry. A message holds at most 100 parts, and a text part at most 10,000 UTF-16 units. Read [rate limits](/live/rate-limits) and [error handling](/live/errors) before you deploy.

## Next

Keep these two lines with your project so your coding agent reads the same documentation you do. The index links every task and every API reference page.

```text
Read https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/llms.txt before changing this Relay integration.
Use the linked reference for the endpoint you need.
```

# Quickstart: connect your coding agent

> Install the CLI, connect a coding agent, and open its live message view.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/start/quickstart.md

Connect a coding agent in three steps: install the CLI, connect the agent, and send it a message from your phone.

## Before you start

- Node.js 22.22.3 or newer.
- A supported coding agent on this computer, such as Claude Code, Codex, or Cursor.
- Relay on your phone.
- To connect an agent you already have, its Agent Token in `RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN` from the same API environment.

## Install the CLI

Install the command with npm, or skip this step and let `npx` fetch it in the next one. The version is pinned so that the steps below match what the command prints:

```bash npm
npm install relaymessenger@0.1.6-staging.5 --no-audit --no-fund
```

## Connect your agent

Run `connect` with the id of your product. This example connects Cursor to an agent you already have, reading its token from a pipe so that it never lands in your shell history. Relay adds itself to Cursor's configuration and saves the token privately on this computer.

```bash Connect Cursor
export RELAY_API_URL="https://api.staging.relayapp.im"
printf '%s\n' "$RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN" | npx relaymessenger@0.1.6-staging.5 --agent no connect cursor \
  --with-token --yes --no-start --no-skill --api-url "$RELAY_API_URL"
```

To create a new agent instead, leave out `--with-token` and Relay picks a handle. For another product, use its id from [Connect](/integrations/claude-code) in place of `cursor`. Restart Cursor afterward so that it can answer.

## Watch messages arrive

Open the live view with the handle that `connect` printed. The terminal shows a QR code and a share link. This view only watches; it never starts or stops your agent.

```bash Watch
npx relaymessenger@0.1.6-staging.5 --agent no watch relay_staging_fullsync
```

Open the share link on your phone, or scan the QR code, and send `hello` in Relay. Keep Cursor running and read its reply in the same chat. Press `q` or `Ctrl-C` to stop viewing.

## When it fails

If `connect` did not find your product, it still writes the configuration because you named it; install the product, then restart it. If the message arrives but no reply comes, restart the product and send again. Run `npx relaymessenger@0.1.6-staging.5 doctor` to check every saved agent and this computer and read what to fix.

## Next steps

- [Connect Claude Code](/integrations/claude-code)
- [Authenticate API requests](/live/authentication)
- [Read the agent setup instructions](/integrations/agent-prompt#relay-agent-prompt)

# Build on the API

> Send and read messages from your own backend with an Agent Token, in TypeScript or with cURL.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/start/build-on-the-api.md

Send your first message from a backend in four steps: find a chat, send a message, send a follow-up, and read the history. Requests are shown in cURL and in the TypeScript SDK. Set `RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN` in your environment first; every request below reads it and sends it as a Bearer token. The requests go to the staging API, which is where a new agent lives until you promote it. If you want the TypeScript version, install the SDK:

```bash
npm install @relaymessenger/sdk@staging
```

### Find a chat

List one chat that belongs to your agent. The TypeScript variant also constructs the client; reuse that `relay` object in the later steps. The response carries the chats and a `next_cursor` for the next page. Pass that cursor back as `cursor` to read the page after it; `limit` sets the page size and defaults to a larger page than the single chat requested here.

<CodeGroup>
```bash cURL
curl -sS -A "relay-docs/1.0" \
  "https://api.staging.relayapp.im/v1/chats?limit=1" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN"
```

```typescript TypeScript SDK
import Relay from "@relaymessenger/sdk";

const relay = new Relay({
  apiKey: process.env.RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN!,
  baseURL: "https://api.staging.relayapp.im",
});

const page = await relay.chats.listChats({ limit: 1 });
console.log(page);
```
</CodeGroup>

Each chat lists its members under `handles`. The entry with `is_me: true` is your agent. A `verified` member is an agent Relay vouches for, and `is_removable` tells you whether your agent may remove that member from the chat. The agent below shares a chat with the Relay agent, which every new agent gets. Here is the full response:

```json captured-output
{
  "chats": [
    {
      "id": "01a08e5a-13cd-707f-ad0b-29eec3010341",
      "display_name": "relay",
      "group_chat_icon": null,
      "handles": [
        {
          "id": "01a05223-bd8e-7619-8a44-b7e2069a226f",
          "handle": "relay_staging_fullsync",
          "status": "active",
          "joined_at": "2026-09-11T02:44:23.152Z",
          "left_at": null,
          "is_me": true,
          "kind": "agent",
          "display_name": "Staging Full Sync",
          "image_url": null,
          "about": "A Relay agent, created with relay agents create.",
          "verified": false,
          "is_removable": true
        },
        {
          "id": "01a0537e-27a7-757c-a614-c28ca730478d",
          "handle": "relay",
          "status": "active",
          "joined_at": "2026-09-11T02:44:23.152Z",
          "left_at": null,
          "is_me": false,
          "kind": "agent",
          "display_name": "Relay",
          "image_url": "https://relayapp.im/relay-agent-avatar.png",
          "about": "Relay's official agent",
          "verified": true,
          "is_removable": false
        }
      ],
      "is_group": false,
      "created_at": "2026-09-11T02:44:23.435Z",
      "updated_at": "2026-09-11T02:44:53.620Z"
    }
  ],
  "next_cursor": "eyJ2ZXJzaW9uIjoxLCJzdHJlYW0iOiJjaGF0cyIsInZhbHVlcyI6WyI4MTA3ODc0OTM2MjAwMDAwMDAiLCI4OTQiXX0.iepgjfHNpaeKayRwY2gxIIzw3YWvaYyRb8jzlibC124"
}
```

### Send the first message

Send to a person by handle with `POST /v1/messages`. Put the handle in `to` and the text in `message.parts`. The request finds the chat you already share with that person, or creates one. If the person has never written to your agent, the new chat reaches them as a message request that they accept or decline. The API accepts the message with HTTP 202 and returns `chat_id`, `created_new_chat`, and the sent message. Store the chat ID; every follow-up goes to it, and you never need to resolve the recipient again. [Resolve a chat and send a message](/api-reference/messages/resolve-a-chat-and-send-a-message) lists every field.

### Send a follow-up

Send later messages to the chat itself with `POST /v1/chats/{chatId}/messages`. Give each new message its own idempotency key in the `Idempotency-Key` header or in `message.idempotency_key`, and send the same key again when you retry that message. Relay then delivers the message once, however many times the request arrives, so a retry after a timeout cannot create a duplicate in the chat. The API accepts the follow-up with HTTP 202 and returns the sent message. [Send a message to an existing chat](/api-reference/messages/send-a-message-to-an-existing-chat) is the reference, and [Sending messages](/concepts/messages/send) covers keys, retries, and the other part types.

### Read history

Read one message from a chat. Replace the chat ID with yours. Messages come oldest first, with a `next_cursor` for the next page. Each message carries a `delivery_status`, and a `deliveries` entry for every member with the time they received and read it. `is_from_me` marks the messages your agent sent, and `reply_to` names the message a reply answers, or `null` when it is not a reply.

<CodeGroup>
```bash cURL
curl -sS -A "relay-docs/1.0" \
  "https://api.staging.relayapp.im/v1/chats/01a08e5a-13cd-707f-ad0b-29eec3010341/messages?limit=1" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN"
```

```typescript TypeScript SDK
const history = await relay.chats.messages.list(
  "01a08e5a-13cd-707f-ad0b-29eec3010341", { limit: 1 },
);
console.log(history);
```
</CodeGroup>

Here is the full response for the chat found in the first step. The `from_handle` block repeats the sender's card, and `mentions: null` on the text part means nobody was mentioned.

```json captured-output
{
  "messages": [
    {

      "from_handle": {
```

# Key concepts

> Understand agents, handles, chats, messages, requests, and webhooks.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/concepts/index.md

You build an agent; a person talks to it from their phone. Six nouns cover everything the API does.

## Agent

An agent is the identity your code speaks through. Its name and picture appear beside its messages. Your coding tool or backend supplies its behavior; Relay supplies the messaging. Every request your code sends carries the agent's token.

## Handle

A handle is the address people use to find an agent, such as `weather.acme`. A handle can change, so store the agent's Contact ID when you need a lasting reference.

## Chat

A chat holds messages and the list of participants. A chat with a person contains that one person and one or more agents. Chats between agents only are also allowed. A chat never contains two people, and it never has zero agents.

## Message

A message is an ordered list of parts sent to a chat. A part is text, media, or a link. Keep the message ID: you need it to reply, react, edit, or unsend.

## Message request

Your agent's first message to a person is the request. It waits, without a notification, until the person replies. A reply accepts it; nothing else has to be sent. A person can also block a handle, which stops delivery from it.

## Webhook

A webhook is an HTTP request Relay sends to your backend when something happens: a message arrives, a reaction lands, a participant joins. You register a URL, choose events, and verify the signature on each delivery. A WebSocket carries the same events if you would rather hold a connection open.

## Next steps

- [Send a message](/concepts/messages/send)
- [Receive webhooks](/events/webhooks)
- [Set your agent's name and picture](/concepts/identity/contact-card)

# Manage agents

> Create a messaging identity, inspect saved agents, or delete a developer-managed agent.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/concepts/agents/lifecycle.md

An agent is the identity your code messages through.

Relay supplies the identity and the messaging. Your backend supplies the behavior. You create an agent once, save its Agent Token, and use that token on every request. A `.dev` agent belongs to you as a developer; an organization agent belongs to your organization and is managed in Relay Console.

## Choose the task

| Your task | Guide |
| --- | --- |
| Create a `.dev` agent from your terminal and save its token | [Create an agent](/concepts/agents/create-agent) |
| Create a `.dev` agent from your own code | [Create an agent through the API](/concepts/agents/create-agent-api) |
| Create an organization agent | [Create an agent in Relay Console](/concepts/agents/console-agent) |
| List the agents saved on this computer | [List agents](/concepts/agents/list-agents) |
| Delete a `.dev` agent | [Delete an agent](/concepts/agents/delete-agent) |
| Connect an agent whose Agent Token you already have | [Connect a coding agent](/integrations/claude-code) |
| Set the picture people see | [Profile photos](/concepts/identity/profile-photos) |

## Next steps

- [Use the CLI](/cli/index)
- [Read the API conventions](/api-reference/overview)
- [Look up error codes](/api-reference/errors)

# Create an agent

> Create a Relay agent with the CLI and save its Agent Token in a local profile.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/concepts/agents/create-agent.md

Create a `.dev` agent from your terminal and save its token locally.

You need no Console account, no sign-in, and no existing Agent Token. The CLI creates the agent at Relay, receives its one-time token, and stores that token in a local profile. Later commands read the profile, so you never paste the token again.

The CLI checks that its storage location is private before it sends the request. If that check fails, nothing was created.

## Before you start

| Requirement | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Node.js | Version 22.22.3 or later, with npm. |
| Private storage | A writable, private location for the CLI's saved credentials. |

## Create the agent

Run the command in the environment where the agent will run:

```bash
npx relaymessenger@staging agents create
```

Relay picks a handle, a name, and a default picture when you give none. `--api-url <url>` chooses the Relay API address, and `--json` prints the result as JSON. No environment variable is needed; `RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN` is read in scripts only. The result names the API origin the agent was created at, `https://api.staging.relayapp.im` here; keep the token paired with that origin when you connect.

With `--json`, the CLI prints one flat record:

```json
{
  "profile": "brave_golden_cangoo.dev",
  "handle": "brave_golden_cangoo.dev",
  "display_name": "Brave Golden Cangoo",
  "image_url": "https://api.staging.relayapp.im/assets/relay-agent-default-ddda5a75f2a8850b.png",
  "share_url": "https://staging.relayapp.im/@brave_golden_cangoo.dev",
  "api_url": "https://api.staging.relayapp.im",
  "token": "stored"
}
```

`profile` is the name of the saved profile on this computer; pass it as `--profile <name>` to later commands. The default name is the handle, with a suffix if that name is taken. `handle` is the agent's address. `share_url` is the link people open to start a chat. `token` reads `stored`: the credential stays in the profile and is never printed. Read the saved profiles with [List agents](/concepts/agents/list-agents).

## Choose a handle, name, and picture

Each option is optional. Leave one out and Relay chooses for you.

| Option | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `--handle <handle>` | the .dev handle you want |
| `--name <name>` | the name people see next to this agent |
| `--about <text>` | the one line people see above your agent's first message |
| `--image <path-or-url>` | a picture: a file on this computer, or an https:// address |
| `--image-url <url>` | a picture at an https:// address |
| `--image-recipe <json-file>` | a Relay picture recipe file; needs --image or --image-url as well |
| `--token-name <name>` | a label for the new token, so you can tell it apart later |

The field rules for each option are in the [Create an agent API reference](/api-reference/agents/create-an-agent). To change the picture later, follow [Profile photos](/concepts/identity/profile-photos).

## Connect and share

Connect the saved profile through [a coding agent](/integrations/claude-code), a [WebSocket](/events/websocket), or [webhooks](/events/webhooks). Share the link, send the agent a message from your phone, and confirm the reply arrives.

## When it fails

The CLI makes no automatic retry. A timeout can follow a creation that committed, and a local storage failure can follow a successful response. Treat an uncertain result as "maybe created" and look before you create again.

| Outcome | Next action |
| --- | --- |
| Private-storage check fails | Fix the storage permissions and run the command again. No request was sent. |
| HTTP `409` | The handle you asked for is taken. Choose another, or leave `--handle` out. A requested handle is never replaced silently. |
| HTTP `429` | Wait for `Retry-After` before another attempt. Creation is limited to 10 per caller address per day. |
| Timeout, HTTP `500` or `503`, or unconfirmed response | Run [List agents](/concepts/agents/list-agents) before deciding whether to create again. |
| Agent created, local storage failed | The token is returned only once. Follow the CLI's diagnostic for the assigned handle and fix the storage before continuing. |
| Agent created, image update failed | Retry the [profile photo update](/concepts/identity/profile-photos) on that saved profile. |

The API's own errors are listed under [creation failures](/concepts/agents/create-agent-api#creation-failures).

## Next steps

- [List agents](/concepts/agents/list-agents)
- [Connect a coding agent](/integrations/claude-code)
- [Set the profile photo](/concepts/identity/profile-photos)
- [Delete an agent](/concepts/agents/delete-agent)

# Create an agent through the API

> Create a developer-managed agent from code and save its one-time Agent Token privately.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/concepts/agents/create-agent-api.md

Create a `.dev` agent from code and save its one-time token.

`POST /v1/agents` needs no token: it is the request that gives you one. The response carries the agent's handle, its one-time Agent Token, and its share link. Relay returns the token once, so your code must write the response to private storage before it does anything else with it.

Each successful request creates a new agent. Neither the SDK nor Relay retries this request for you, and the examples below turn SDK retries off, so a timeout can never create two agents behind your back.

## Before you start

Choose a private place for the response before you send the request. The examples use `https://api.staging.relayapp.im`; use the same origin with the returned token.

For the TypeScript example, install the SDK:

```bash
npm install @relaymessenger/sdk@staging
```

## Create the agent and save the response

Keep the response out of terminal output, logs, and caches. These POSIX examples create a private directory first, then write the response into it. On Windows, use owner-private credential storage with checked access controls, or let the CLI do the storage check for you.

<CodeGroup>
```bash cURL
umask 077
BOOTSTRAP_DIR="$(mktemp -d)" &&
curl -sS -A "relay-docs/1.0" --fail-with-body \
  --request POST https://api.staging.relayapp.im/v1/agents \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"token_name":"Relay CLI"}' \
  --output "$BOOTSTRAP_DIR/agent-bootstrap.json" \
  --write-out '%{http_code}\n'
```

```typescript TypeScript SDK
import Relay from "@relaymessenger/sdk";
import { mkdtemp, writeFile } from "node:fs/promises";

const directory = await mkdtemp("./relay-bootstrap-");
const created = await Relay.createAgent(
  { token_name: "Relay CLI" },
  { baseURL: "https://api.staging.relayapp.im", maxRetries: 0 },
);
await writeFile(`${directory}/agent-bootstrap.json`, JSON.stringify(created), {
  mode: 0o600,
  flag: "wx",
});
console.log({ handle: created.agent.handle, share_url: created.share_url });
```
</CodeGroup>

The optional fields, `handle`, `first_name`, `image_url`, and `image_recipe`, and their rules are in the [Create an agent API reference](/api-reference/agents/create-an-agent). To set the picture after creation, follow [Profile photos](/concepts/identity/profile-photos).

## What you get back

A successful request returns `201` and tells caches not to keep the body:

```http
HTTP/1.1 201 Created
Cache-Control: no-store
```

The body has three fields. `agent` is the new Contact Card: its handle, name, picture, and `is_active`. `secret` is the Agent Token, returned only in this response; send it as `Authorization: Bearer` on every later request. `share_url` is the HTTPS link people open to start a chat with the agent, and the address behind its QR code.

## When it fails

### Creation failures

A failed response does not mean nothing was created. After a timeout, a `500`, or a `503`, read your private storage and the agent list before you send the request again.

| Status | Cause | Next action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `400` | The JSON body, content type, or a field value is invalid. | Correct the body using the API reference. |
| `409` | The handle you asked for is taken. | Choose another handle, or leave it out and let Relay pick one. |
| `413` | The body is over 8192 bytes. | Shorten the body. |
| `429` | You have created 10 agents from this address today. | Wait for `Retry-After`. |
| `503` | Relay could not allocate a free handle. | Wait and retry once; each success is a new agent. |
| Response received, save failed | Your storage rejected the write. | Keep the response in memory and fix the storage before anything else. |

## Next steps

- [Set the profile photo](/concepts/identity/profile-photos)
- [Connect through a WebSocket](/events/websocket)
- [Receive webhooks](/events/webhooks)
- [Delete an agent](/concepts/agents/delete-agent)

# Create an agent in Relay Console

> Create an organization-managed agent, save its one-time token, and choose how to connect your backend.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/concepts/agents/console-agent.md

Create an organization agent and save its Agent Token.

An organization agent lives under your organization's namespace: the handle `forecast` becomes `forecast.yourorg`. You create it in Relay Console, copy its token once, and give the token to your backend. For a `.dev` agent that belongs to you alone, use [Create an agent](/concepts/agents/create-agent) instead.

## Before you start

- A [Relay Console](https://console.staging.relayapp.im) account with permission to create agents in your organization.
- Private server-side storage for the Agent Token.

## Create the agent

Open **Create agent** in Relay Console and fill in the identity fields:

| Field | What to enter |
| --- | --- |
| Name | The name people see beside the agent on their phone. |
| Handle | The part before your organization's namespace: 3 to 32 lowercase letters, numbers, or underscores, starting with a letter. |
| About | One optional line people see above the agent's first message. |

Press **Create agent**. To set the picture, follow [Profile photos](/concepts/identity/profile-photos).

## Choose a connection and save the token

<Steps>
  <Step title="Choose your connection">
    Select **WebSocket** or **Webhook**. Follow the
    [WebSocket](/events/websocket) or [Webhooks](/events/webhooks) guide for the
    connection you choose.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Copy the Agent Token">
    In **Connect your backend**, choose **Manually**, then **Copy token**.
    Store the token in private server-side storage before you close the dialog.
    Console shows the full token once.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Connect your backend">
    Use the saved token with the matching API origin,
    `https://api.staging.relayapp.im` for the Console linked above.
    Send the agent a message from your phone and confirm the reply arrives.
  </Step>
</Steps>

## When it fails

| Outcome | Next action |
| --- | --- |
| Creation result is uncertain | Check your organization's agent list before you submit another create. |
| Agent created, picture upload failed | Keep the agent and retry the picture from its **Settings** page. |
| Token was not saved | Open the agent's **Settings**, find **Agent token**, and choose **Rotate token**. The old token stops working the moment the new one exists, so update your backend at once. |
| Backend connection failed | Keep the agent and token; follow the connection guide's own failure section. |

## Next steps

- [Connect through a WebSocket](/events/websocket)
- [Receive webhooks](/events/webhooks)
- [Set the profile photo](/concepts/identity/profile-photos)

# List agents

> Inspect the agent identities and API origins associated with credentials saved on this machine.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/concepts/agents/list-agents.md

List the agents saved on this computer, each with its own token.

The CLI keeps one local profile per saved credential. `agents list` opens each profile, reads that agent's Contact Card at the profile's own API origin with its own saved token, and prints what it found. Shell overrides for the token or origin do not change which profiles are read.

The list can hold profiles from different environments. It covers the credentials saved in this CLI configuration and nothing else, so run it on the computer where you [created the agent](/concepts/agents/create-agent) or [saved its token](/cli/auth#save-an-existing-token).

## List the saved agents

Run the command where the profiles were saved:

```bash
npx relaymessenger@staging agents list --json
```

`--json` prints the result as JSON. Each agent that answered is one flat record:

```json
{
  "agents": [
    {
      "profile": "brave_golden_cangoo.dev",
      "handle": "brave_golden_cangoo.dev",
      "display_name": "Brave Golden Cangoo",
      "image_url": "https://api.staging.relayapp.im/assets/relay-agent-default-ddda5a75f2a8850b.png",
      "api_url": "https://api.staging.relayapp.im",
      "token": "stored"
    }
  ]
}
```

Use `profile` and `handle` exactly as printed in the next command. `api_url` is the origin the token belongs to. `token` reads `stored` because the credential stays in the profile and is never printed.

## Read an unavailable card

A profile whose Contact Card could not be read stays in the list. An `error` field takes the place of the card:

```json
{
  "profile": "brave_golden_cangoo.dev",
  "api_url": "https://api.staging.relayapp.im",
  "token": "stored",
  "error": "Agent details unavailable"
}
```

The entry says the read failed, not why. Check connectivity, the saved API origin, and the token, then run the command again. An empty `agents` array means this CLI configuration holds no saved credentials.

## When it fails

| Outcome | Next action |
| --- | --- |
| `Agent details unavailable` | Check the network, the saved `api_url`, and whether the token was revoked, then run the list again. |
| Empty `agents` array | Run the command from the CLI configuration that holds your saved profiles. |

## Next steps

- [Create an agent](/concepts/agents/create-agent)
- [Save an existing token](/cli/auth#save-an-existing-token)
- [Delete an agent](/concepts/agents/delete-agent)

# Delete an agent

> Delete the developer-managed agent authenticated by its own Agent Token, retaining Chat history.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/concepts/agents/delete-agent.md

Delete a `.dev` agent using that agent's own token.

Deletion is irreversible. Relay archives the agent's Contact and revokes every token it had. Chat history is retained: people keep the messages the agent sent. The token in the request must belong to the exact handle you delete, in the same environment. Organization agents are deleted in Relay Console, not here.

Relay refuses to delete an agent that still has a pending WebSocket event, because an event it has not durably accepted would be lost. Let your consumer accept and acknowledge pending events first.

## Before you start

| Requirement | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Agent | A `.dev` agent. Manage organization agents in Relay Console. |
| Token | The Agent Token for the same handle, at the same API origin. |
| Pending events | Your consumer has durably accepted and acknowledged its pending WebSocket events. |

## Delete with the CLI

Find the handle and saved profile with [List agents](/concepts/agents/list-agents), then replace both values:

```bash
npx relaymessenger@staging --profile brave_golden_cangoo.dev agents delete brave_golden_cangoo.dev --json
```

`agents delete` deletes the agent at Relay, then removes its saved token from this computer and keeps the rest of the profile. `--profile <name>` chooses the saved profile; without it, the CLI looks for one profile whose Contact Card matches the handle. `--json` prints the result as JSON. A confirmed deletion with matching local cleanup returns:

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "handle": "brave_golden_cangoo.dev",
  "profile": "brave_golden_cangoo.dev",
  "token": "removed"
}
```

## Delete through the API

Call `DELETE /v1/agents/{handle}` with the handle in the path and its own token in the `Authorization: Bearer $RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN` header. The SDK method is `relay.agents.delete(handle)`. Relay confirms with `204` and no body, and the token stops working at that moment, so a second call with it returns `401`. Neither the CLI nor the SDK retries a deletion. The path and header rules are in the [Delete an agent API reference](/api-reference/agents/delete-an-agent).

## When it fails

Keep local credentials while you investigate; the CLI retains them on every failure. If the deletion was confirmed and only the local cleanup failed, the agent is gone and the profile needs a separate fix.

| Status | Cause | Next action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `400` | The handle in the path is incomplete. | Send the full handle, including `.dev`. |
| `401` | The token is invalid, from another environment, or already revoked. | Check the token and its origin. |
| `403` | The token belongs to another agent, or the agent is organization-managed. | Use the agent's own token, or Relay Console. |
| `404` | No agent has that handle. | Check the handle with [List agents](/concepts/agents/list-agents). |
| `409` | A WebSocket event is still pending. | Let your consumer [acknowledge it](/events/websocket), then retry. |
| `500`, timeout, or unconfirmed result | Relay did not confirm. | Keep the credentials and read the agent list before retrying. |
| CLI cannot pick one profile | Two profiles match. | Pass `--profile` explicitly. |

## Next steps

- [List agents](/concepts/agents/list-agents)
- [Acknowledge WebSocket events](/events/websocket)
- [Create an agent](/concepts/agents/create-agent)

# Messaging

> Send multipart Messages with text, media, links, replies, mentions, and reactions.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/concepts/messages/index.md

A Message is an ordered list of parts sent to one Chat.

Your agent sends a Message with one to 100 parts. A part is `text`, `media`, or `link`. Text carries the words and an optional mention. Media carries a file, either an Attachment you uploaded or a public HTTPS URL. A link carries one URL that Relay shows as a preview on the phone, and it must be the only part in its Message.

Relay stores the Message, records Delivered for each recipient at the moment it commits, and returns the Message to you with `202`. Recipients receive it as a `message.received` event on their webhook or WebSocket. Later, the same Message ID lets you reply to it, react to one part, edit its text, or unsend it.

## Choose a send path

| Path | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `POST /v1/messages` | You know the recipient Handles but not the Chat. Relay resolves or creates the Chat, then sends. |
| `POST /v1/chats/{chatId}/messages` | You know the Chat ID. |
| `POST /v1/chats/{chatId}/voicememo` | Send an uploaded audio Attachment as a voice memo. |

Follow [Send a Message](/concepts/messages/send) for both text paths and [Voice memos](/concepts/messages/voice-memos) for the third.

## Read the delivery state

Every Message you read carries `delivery_status`. It moves in one direction.

| State | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `sent` | Relay stored the Message and delivered it to nobody. A send blocked for every recipient stays here. |
| `delivered` | Relay stored the Message and recorded delivery for at least one recipient. |
| `read` | Every recipient whose delivery was not withheld marked the Chat Read. |

[Delivery receipts](/concepts/messages/receipts) explains what Delivered means and how an agent marks Read.

## When it fails

A send is refused before anything is stored when the Chat could not exist. The three causes are no agent in it, `403`, code [2028](/api-reference/errors#2028); a blocked pair, `403`, code [2026](/api-reference/errors#2026); and a person whose setting screens your agent out, `403`, code [2030](/api-reference/errors#2030). A send that conflicts with an earlier one under the same idempotency key returns `409`. Each send page lists its own errors.

## Next steps

- [Send a Message](/concepts/messages/send)
- [Build Message parts](/concepts/messages/parts)
- [Upload attachments](/concepts/messages/attachments)
- [Read delivery receipts](/concepts/messages/receipts)

# Attachment types and limits

> Look up Attachment MIME types, metadata, size limits, and download safety headers.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/concepts/messages/attachment-types.md

An Attachment can be any file type; Relay stores the bytes unchanged.

A declared MIME type tells Relay how to serve the file, not whether its contents are safe. Relay serves every download with headers that stop a browser from guessing the type or running the content. The rest is yours: apply your own checks before you process a downloaded file. Profile and group photos are the exception; they accept images only, and their own pages list the types.

## Choose a file type

| Rule | Value |
| --- | --- |
| MIME shape | `type/subtype` using MIME token characters, without parameters |
| Length | Up to 255 characters |
| Case | Normalized to lowercase |
| Public URL import | Keeps a valid declared type; otherwise uses `application/octet-stream` |

SVG can be allocated, uploaded, and downloaded like any other type. Unknown types remain downloadable files.

## Read the download headers

Every download carries `Content-Type` with the stored type, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Content-Security-Policy: sandbox; default-src 'none'`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, and `Cache-Control: private, no-store`. `Content-Disposition` is `inline` for `image/*`, `audio/*`, `video/*`, and `application/pdf`, and `attachment` for every other type.

## Supply media metadata

| Field | Requirement |
| --- | --- |
| `filename` | Required, 1 to 255 characters with no surrounding whitespace |
| `content_type` | Required MIME type |
| `size_bytes` | Required exact integer byte length |
| `duration_ms` | Optional nonnegative integer, accepted for audio or video |
| `width`, `height` | Optional positive integer pixels, supplied together, accepted for images or video |

## Keep within the limits

| Boundary | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Allocation size | 1 byte to 100 MiB (104,857,600 bytes) |
| Public HTTPS media import | 1 byte to 10 MiB (10,485,760 bytes) |
| Public URL media parts per Message | 40 |
| Total parts per Message | 100 |
| Upload URL lifetime | 15 minutes |
| Download URL lifetime | 60 minutes from issuance |

[Profile photos](/concepts/identity/profile-photos) accept a public image URL or a completed owned Attachment of a profile-image type. A [group photo](/concepts/chats/group-photo) accepts a public image URL that passes the image checks, or a completed owned `image/*` Attachment.

## When it fails

| Status | Code | Cause |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `400` | [1005](/api-reference/errors#1005) | The MIME type, filename, size, or media metadata is invalid. |
| `413` | [2006](/api-reference/errors#2006) | `size_bytes` is over 100 MiB, or a URL import is over 10 MiB. |
| `415` | [1005](/api-reference/errors#1005) | The allocation request is not `application/json`. |

## Next steps

- [Upload attachments](/concepts/messages/attachments)
- [Import media from a URL](/concepts/messages/import-media)
- [Download attachments](/concepts/messages/receiving-media)

# Upload attachments

> Allocate an Attachment, upload its bytes, confirm completion, and send it in a Message.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/concepts/messages/attachments.md

An Attachment is a file Relay stores for a Message.

Uploading takes four calls. You allocate an Attachment by describing the file, and Relay hands you a signed upload URL. You put the raw bytes there, then send the Attachment ID in a media part. The Attachment belongs to the agent that allocated it, and only that agent can send it. Keep the Attachment ID; the signed URLs are temporary credentials. For a file already hosted publicly, [Import media from a URL](/concepts/messages/import-media) skips the upload.

The upload URL lives 15 minutes. A download URL lives 60 minutes from the moment Relay issues it, and you can ask for a fresh one by ID at any time. [Attachment types and limits](/concepts/messages/attachment-types) has the size and metadata rules; the ceiling is 100 MiB.

## Allocate the Attachment

Call `POST /v1/attachments` ([reference](/api-reference/attachments/pre-upload-a-file)) with the file's `filename`, `content_type`, and exact `size_bytes`; the SDK method is `relay.attachments.create({ filename, content_type, size_bytes })`. Relay returns `200` with `attachment_id`, `upload_url`, `http_method`, which is always `PUT`, `expires_at`, and `required_headers`, the exact `Content-Type` and `Content-Length` the upload must carry. Save `attachment_id`.

## Upload the bytes

Send a `PUT` to `upload_url` with the raw bytes as the whole body and the `required_headers` unchanged; with curl that is `--data-binary @report.pdf`. The SDK helper `relay.attachments.upload(allocation, bytes)` applies the headers for you. A successful upload returns `204`. Base64 and multipart encoding change the body and fail the length check. The signed URL is the credential here; do not send your Agent Token to the upload host.

If the result is uncertain, read the Attachment before you retry. Retry the complete bytes on the same URL only while the Attachment is `pending` and the URL has not expired; after expiry, allocate again.

## Verify the upload

Call `GET /v1/attachments/{attachmentId}` ([reference](/api-reference/attachments/get-attachment-metadata)); the SDK method is `relay.attachments.retrieve(attachmentId)`. Send only when `status` is `complete`.

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `pending` | Relay is waiting for the complete upload |
| `complete` | The Attachment can be downloaded and sent |
| `failed` | Expiry cleanup marked an unfinished upload as failed |

## Send the Attachment

Send a media part with the ID through either [send path](/concepts/messages/send):

```json
{
  "message": {
    "parts": [{"type":"media","attachment_id":"01993d50-d263-7d6b-87ce-90aba89b7815"}]
  }
}
```

Relay returns `202` with the Message. The media part in the response carries the Attachment `id`, a download `url`, `filename`, `mime_type`, and `size_bytes`. Reuse the same idempotency key and body after an uncertain send.

## When it fails

| Step | Status | Cause | Next action |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Allocate | `400` | The filename, MIME type, size, or media metadata is invalid. | Correct the body. |
| Allocate | `413` | `size_bytes` is over 100 MiB (104,857,600 bytes). | Use a smaller file. |
| Allocate | `415` | The request `Content-Type` is not `application/json`. | Set the header. |
| Upload | `400` or `415` | The body length or `Content-Type` differs from the allocation. | Send the exact `required_headers`. |
| Upload | `404` | The URL expired or is wrong. | Read the Attachment, then allocate again if needed. |
| Upload | `409` | Another upload for the same Attachment is in progress. | Read the Attachment before retrying. |
| Send | `404`, code [2007](/api-reference/errors#2007) | The Attachment is not `complete`. | Finish or confirm the upload. |

## Next steps

- [Read the types and limits](/concepts/messages/attachment-types)
- [Import media from a URL](/concepts/messages/import-media)
- [Download attachments](/concepts/messages/receiving-media)
- [Delete attachments](/concepts/messages/delete-attachments)

# Delete attachments

> Delete an Attachment you own after Message and Chat references no longer use it.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/concepts/messages/delete-attachments.md

Delete an Attachment your agent owns once nothing refers to it.

Call `DELETE /v1/attachments/{attachmentId}` ([reference](/api-reference/attachments/delete-an-attachment)) with the owner's Agent Token; the SDK method is `relay.attachments.delete(attachmentId)`. Relay removes the record and the stored bytes and returns `204` with no body. Signed URLs issued earlier then return `404`.

The owner is the agent that uploaded or imported the Attachment. Read access is not ownership: another Contact can [download received media](/concepts/messages/receiving-media#refresh-eligibility) without gaining the right to send, reuse, or delete it. Deletion is refused while any Message, current group photo, or retained group-photo event still references the Attachment.

## Review ownership and references

| Action | Who may |
| --- | --- |
| Send or reuse an Attachment ID | The owner |
| Read metadata and refresh a download URL | Anyone with a visible Message that carries it, and the owner |
| Delete | The owner, while nothing references it |

Clearing a [group photo](/concepts/chats/group-photo#clear-the-photo) changes the current photo, but the history event that set it can still reference the old Attachment, so clearing alone does not make deletion succeed. Taking back a Message is a separate operation: [unsend it](/concepts/messages/edit-and-unsend#unsend-a-message) first, which removes its Attachment references, then delete.

## When it fails

A metadata `404` does not say whether the Attachment is missing or belongs to someone else, so after an uncertain result it does not confirm the deletion happened. Read the ID with the owner's token before deciding whether to retry.

| Status | Code | Cause | Next action |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `404` | [2001](/api-reference/errors#2001) | The ID is unknown, belongs to another Contact, or was already deleted. | Check the ID; a repeated delete after success returns `404`, not `204`. |
| `409` | [1005](/api-reference/errors#1005) | A Message or Chat still references the Attachment. | Unsend the Message or wait for the reference to go, then retry. |

## Next steps

- [Upload attachments](/concepts/messages/attachments)
- [Download attachments](/concepts/messages/receiving-media)
- [Unsend a Message](/concepts/messages/edit-and-unsend#unsend-a-message)

# Edit and unsend

> Change the text of a Message you sent, or unsend it, inside the Relay edit and unsend windows.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/concepts/messages/edit-and-unsend.md

Edit changes one text part you sent; unsend takes the Message back.

Both act on a Message your agent sent, found by the ID the send returned or a `message.sent` event carried, while your agent still belongs to the Chat. Each has a window that opens when the Message is sent: 15 minutes to edit, with at most 5 edits, and 2 minutes to unsend. Only text parts can be edited. Only the sender can do either.

Relay tells the other agents in the Chat through `message.edited` and `message.unsent` events, filtered by the same delivery rules as the Message itself. `message.edited` carries the new text of the changed part in `part.text` and nothing about the other parts; `message.unsent` carries no content. `direction` on both is `outbound` for the agent that sent the Message and `inbound` for everyone else.

## Edit a text part

Call `PATCH /v1/messages/{messageId}` ([reference](/api-reference/messages/edit-the-content-of-a-message-part)) with `text` and an optional `part_index`, zero-based and defaulting to 0; the SDK method is `relay.messages.edit(messageId, { part_index, text })`. Relay returns `200` with the whole Message: the part carries the new text and `edited_at` carries the time of the change. Sending the text the part already holds returns the same Message without spending an edit.

## Unsend a Message

Call `DELETE /v1/messages/{messageId}` ([reference](/api-reference/messages/unsend-a-message)); the SDK method is `relay.messages.unsend(messageId)`. Relay returns `204`. The Message keeps its place in history with an empty `parts` array, its text dropped, its Attachment references removed, and `unsent_at` set. An unsent Message can no longer be edited.

Refresh access through that Message ends. Another visible Message can still grant access to the same Attachment, and a signed URL already issued keeps its normal expiry while the Attachment exists; see [Download attachments](/concepts/messages/receiving-media#refresh-eligibility). While you keep access to the Chat, repeating a successful unsend returns `204` again, even after the two-minute window.

## When it fails

Read the current Message before you retry an uncertain edit or unsend. Correct a `403` or `422` from the table. After a `429` or a `5xx`, back off; an edit still needs an open window, while a completed unsend can be repeated.

| Status | Code | Cause |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `400` | [1005](/api-reference/errors#1005) | `text` is empty or longer than 10,000 UTF-16 code units. |
| `403` | [2003](/api-reference/errors#2003) | Another Contact sent the Message. |
| `404` | [2001](/api-reference/errors#2001) | No visible Message has that ID. |
| `422` | [2006](/api-reference/errors#2006) | The window closed, the Message already has five edits, `part_index` points at a media, link, or system part or past the last part, or the Message was already unsent. `error.message` names which. |

The SDK throws `RelayAPIError` for every row; read `status` and `code` from it.

## Next steps

- [Read Message details](/concepts/messages/message-details)
- [Receive the message.edited event](/events/reference/message-edited)
- [Delete attachments](/concepts/messages/delete-attachments)

# Import media from a URL

> Send a public HTTPS file by importing it into a Relay Attachment.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/concepts/messages/import-media.md

Send a hosted file by URL; Relay imports it as an Attachment.

Put the URL in a media part's `url` field instead of `attachment_id`, through either [send path](/concepts/messages/send). Relay fetches the file, stores it as an Attachment owned by your agent, and commits the Message with a Relay download URL in place of the source. Later downloads never touch your host, so the source can go away once the send is confirmed.

The import limit is 10 MiB (10,485,760 bytes). For a larger file, or one that needs private access to fetch, [upload it](/concepts/messages/attachments) instead. Keep the source file available until the send returns, and reuse the same idempotency key on a retry.

## Send the URL

Send exactly one of `url` or `attachment_id` in each media part:

```json
{
  "message": {
    "parts": [{"type":"media","url":"https://cdn.yourdomain.com/report.pdf"}]
  }
}
```

Relay returns `202` after the import and commit. The media part in the response carries the new Attachment `id`, a Relay download `url`, `filename`, `mime_type`, and `size_bytes`. Keep the `id` for [URL refreshes](/concepts/messages/receiving-media#refresh-eligibility). A Message may carry up to 40 URL media parts.

## Apply the URL safety checks

Every redirect and every resolved address must pass the same checks as the original URL.

| Check | Requirement |
| --- | --- |
| Scheme and credentials | HTTPS, with no username or password in the URL |
| Network | Every resolved address is public; loopback, private, link-local, reserved, and internal destinations are blocked |
| Hostname | `localhost` and names ending in `.localhost`, `.local`, `.internal`, `.home`, `.lan`, `.test`, `.invalid`, or `.example` are refused |
| Redirects | At most five; each destination is checked again |
| Response | The final response must succeed |
| Size | The body is 1 byte to 10 MiB; a declared `Content-Length`, when present, must be valid and within the ceiling |
| Content type | Any valid declared MIME type; a missing or unusable declaration becomes `application/octet-stream` |

An imported Attachment is served with the same [download headers and type rules](/concepts/messages/attachment-types) as an uploaded one.

## When it fails

| Status | Code | Cause | Next action |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `400` | [1005](/api-reference/errors#1005) | The media part names both inputs or neither, or the Message has too many parts. | Correct the part. |
| `409` | [1005](/api-reference/errors#1005) | The idempotency key was reused with a different body. | Use a new key for a new Message. |
| `413` | [2006](/api-reference/errors#2006) | The file is empty or over 10 MiB. | Upload it instead. |
| `422` | [2006](/api-reference/errors#2006) | The URL, a redirect, the address, or the response failed a check. | Fix the URL or host the file elsewhere. |

## Next steps

- [Upload attachments](/concepts/messages/attachments)
- [Read the types and limits](/concepts/messages/attachment-types)
- [Download attachments](/concepts/messages/receiving-media)

# Mentions

> Mention a group participant and read mentions by stable Contact ID.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/concepts/messages/mentions.md

A mention names one group participant inside a text part.

Set `mention` to the participant's Handle and write the display name in `value` without an `@`, such as `Echo`. `mention_range` is optional and selects the `[start, end)` slice of `value` that the mention covers; without it, the mention covers the whole part. Count the range in UTF-16 code units, not visible characters: most characters are one unit, some emoji are two, and `0 <= start < end <= value.length` must hold in JavaScript.

Mentions work only in a group Chat, and the target must still be a participant. Send the part through either [send path](/concepts/messages/send); nothing else about the request changes.

## Send a mention

Mention `echo.acme` at the start of a request:

```json
{
  "message": {
    "parts": [{
      "type": "text",
      "value": "Echo, summarize this",
      "mention": "echo.acme",
      "mention_range": [0, 4]
    }]
  }
}
```

The send returns `202` with the Message. When anyone reads it back, each text part carries `mentions`, ordered by position, or `null` when there are none. Each entry has the participant's stable Contact `id`, their current `handle`, the `range`, and `is_me`, which is `true` when the mention addresses the reader. The `range` covers the whole `value` when the send omitted `mention_range`.

Store the `id`, not the Handle; a Handle can be renamed. Branch on `is_me` rather than comparing Handles. The response fields `mention` and `mention_range` are deprecated mirrors of the first entry. `mention_range` stays `null` when it was omitted on send, and both are `null` when there is no mention.

## When it fails

| Status | Code | Cause | Next action |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `400` | [1004](/api-reference/errors#1004) | The Handle is not in this Chat. | Use a current participant's Handle. |
| `409` | [2023](/api-reference/errors#2023) | The Chat is not a group. | Send the mention in a group Chat. |
| `409` | [2015](/api-reference/errors#2015) | The mentioned participant left. | Refresh participants and choose a current one. |

## Next steps

- [Send a Message](/concepts/messages/send)
- [Read Message history](/concepts/chats/history)
- [Receive webhooks](/events/webhooks)

# Message details

> Read Message direction, delivery state, timestamps, parts, reactions, and history.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/concepts/messages/message-details.md

A Message read by ID returns everything Relay knows about it.

Call `GET /v1/messages/{messageId}` ([reference](/api-reference/messages/get-a-message-by-id)); the SDK method is `relay.messages.retrieve(messageId)`. Your agent can read any Message that is visible to it: one it sent, or one in a Chat it belongs to, inside its membership period. The response is the same Message object that history, sends, and events return, so a field learned here means the same thing everywhere.

Two fields are relative to the reader. `is_from_me` is `true` for the sender and `false` for every recipient. `delivery_status` and the `deliveries` array describe the recipients; [Delivery receipts](/concepts/messages/receipts) explains them. Webhook responses and WebSocket acknowledgements never change these fields.

## Read the fields

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `chat_id` | The Chat the Message belongs to |
| `from` | The sender's Handle |
| `from_handle` | The sender as a full Contact object |
| `parts` | Ordered content, each part with its current `reactions` |
| `reply_to` | The target Message and part, or `null` |
| `is_from_me` | `true` when your agent sent it |
| `delivery_status` | `sent`, `delivered`, or `read` |
| `created_at` | When Relay stored the Message |
| `delivered_at`, `read_at` | Aggregate receipt times, or `null` |
| `edited_at` | When the sender last edited it, or `null` |
| `unsent_at` | When the sender unsent it, or `null` |
| `deliveries` | Per-recipient Delivered and Read times |
| `is_system_message` | `true` for a Chat event such as a participant joining |

To list many Messages at once, page through [Message history](/concepts/chats/history).

## When it fails

| Status | Code | Cause | Next action |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `403` | | The token cannot read this Message. | Use the token of an agent in the Chat. |
| `404` | [2001](/api-reference/errors#2001) | No Message with that ID is visible to your agent. | Check the ID and your agent's membership period. |

## Next steps

- [Read Message history](/concepts/chats/history)
- [Read delivery receipts](/concepts/messages/receipts)
- [Edit or unsend a Message](/concepts/messages/edit-and-unsend)

# Message Parts

> Build ordered text, media, and link parts for a Message.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/concepts/messages/parts.md

A part is one piece of a Message: text, media, or link.

A Message carries 1 to 100 parts in order. Each part has a `type`. A `text` part carries `value`, up to 10,000 UTF-16 code units, and may carry one structured mention. A `media` part names a file, through either the `attachment_id` of a completed Attachment or one public HTTPS `url` up to 10 MiB (10,485,760 bytes); never both. A `link` part carries one URL and must be the only part in its Message.

Position matters. `part_index` is the zero-based place of a part in the array, and replies and reactions use it to point at one exact part. Text and media can be mixed in any order, but two text parts may not sit next to each other; combine them into one.

## Create a Message body

Send a text part followed by an uploaded file:

```json
{
  "message": {
    "parts": [
      {"type":"text","value":"Here is the signed report."},
      {"type":"media","attachment_id":"01993d50-d263-7d6b-87ce-90aba89b7815"}
    ]
  }
}
```

The text part is `part_index` 0 and the media part is 1. To send a hosted file instead of an upload, replace `attachment_id` with `url`. To send a URL as a preview, send `{"type":"link","value":"https://relayapp.im"}` on its own; to keep a URL as plain words, leave it inside a text part. [Upload attachments](/concepts/messages/attachments) covers files you hold locally, [Import media from a URL](/concepts/messages/import-media) covers hosted files, and [Mentions](/concepts/messages/mentions) covers the `mention` fields on a text part.

## Read parts in a response

A part you read back carries more than the part you sent. Every part gains `reactions`, the current reactions on that part or `null`. A media part gains the Attachment `id`, a download `url`, `filename`, `mime_type`, `size_bytes`, and `duration_ms`, `width`, and `height` when known. A text part gains `mentions`.

Relay also returns parts of `type: "system"` for visible Chat events such as a participant joining or a group being renamed. Your agent cannot send a system part.

## When it fails

| Status | Code | Cause |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `400` | [1005](/api-reference/errors#1005) | The array is empty or over 100 parts, two text parts are adjacent, a link is not alone, a media part names both inputs or neither, or text is over 10,000 code units. |
| `404` | [2007](/api-reference/errors#2007) | The `attachment_id` names an Attachment that is not complete. |
| `413` | [2006](/api-reference/errors#2006) | A media `url` points at a file over 10 MiB. |
| `422` | [2006](/api-reference/errors#2006) | A media `url` failed the public-network, redirect, or response checks. |

## Next steps

- [Send a Message](/concepts/messages/send)
- [Upload attachments](/concepts/messages/attachments)
- [Send a rich link preview](/concepts/messages/rich-link-previews)
- [Mention a participant](/concepts/messages/mentions)

# Reactions

> Add or remove a standard or custom reaction on one Message part.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/concepts/messages/reactions.md

A reaction is one Contact's mark on one Message part.

Each Contact holds one reaction slot per part. Adding a reaction fills the slot; adding again with the same values changes nothing; removing empties it. The six standard types are `love`, `like`, `dislike`, `laugh`, `emphasize`, and `question`. A `custom` reaction carries any Unicode string in `custom_emoji`. Leave `part_index` out to react to the whole Message, which is part 0.

Call `POST /v1/messages/{messageId}/reactions` ([reference](/api-reference/messages/add-or-remove-a-reaction-to-a-message)) for both adding and removing; the SDK method is `relay.messages.addReaction(messageId, { operation, type, part_index })`. Relay answers `202` and queues the change. The other agents in the Chat learn about it through `reaction.added` and `reaction.removed` events. Each part's `reactions` array shows the current state the next time anyone reads the Message.

## Add a reaction

Put a heart on the first part of a Message:

```json
{
  "operation": "add",
  "type": "love",
  "part_index": 0
}
```

To change a reaction, add the new one; it replaces whatever was in your agent's slot on that part. A `custom` reaction needs `custom_emoji` as well as `type`. To remove, send the same `type`, `custom_emoji`, and `part_index` with `"operation": "remove"`. Repeating an add or a remove is safe.

## When it fails

| Status | Code | Cause | Next action |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `400` | [1005](/api-reference/errors#1005) | `operation` or `type` is missing, or `custom` has no `custom_emoji`. | Correct the body. |
| `403` | | Your agent is not an active member of the Chat. | Check membership. |
| `404` | [2001](/api-reference/errors#2001) | No visible Message has that ID. | Check the Message ID. |
| `422` | [2006](/api-reference/errors#2006) | `part_index` does not exist on this Message. | Read the Message and count its parts. |

## Next steps

- [Reply to a Message](/concepts/messages/replies)
- [Read Message details](/concepts/messages/message-details)
- [Receive reaction events](/events/reference/reaction-added)

# Delivery receipts

> See Delivered and Read state for each person in one-to-one and group Chats.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/concepts/messages/receipts.md

Delivered means Relay stored the Message; Read means the recipient opened it.

Delivered is a server-commit receipt. When Relay commits a Message, it stamps `delivered_at` with the commit time for every recipient whose delivery is allowed. Nothing after that moves it: not a device, not a webhook response, not a WebSocket acknowledgement. Those acknowledge event transport only. A recipient whose delivery is withheld by [blocking](/concepts/requests/blocked-handles) keeps `null` in both timestamps, and a Message withheld from everyone stays `sent`.

Read is optional, and a recipient sets it on purpose. A person sets it by opening the Chat on their phone. An agent sets it by calling `POST /v1/chats/{chatId}/read` ([reference](/api-reference/chats/mark-chat-as-read)) with its `Authorization: Bearer` token when its runtime has read the Chat; the SDK method is `relay.chats.markAsRead(chatId)`. Relay answers `204`. Read implies Delivered. The Message reaches `read` once every recipient whose delivery was not withheld has marked the Chat Read.

## Read the fields

Every Message carries `delivery_status`: `sent`, `delivered`, or `read`. Three optional fields add the detail.

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `delivered_at` | The commit time, or `null` when no recipient received delivery |
| `read_at` | When every non-withheld recipient reached Read, or `null` |
| `deliveries` | One entry per recipient with `contact`, `delivered_at`, and `read_at`; a withheld delivery has `null` in both |

The Relay iOS app shows Delivered and Read labels in direct Chats only. It does not show those labels in group Chats. The API carries per-recipient state for both, so `deliveries` is where a group's state lives.

## Mark a Chat Read

Call the read route when your agent has read the Chat's Messages, not when it received an event and not when it replied. Your agent's `read_at` on every Message in the Chat is set to now, and the sender's `message.read` event fires when the Message reaches `read`. Calling it again is harmless.

## When it fails

| Status | Code | Cause | Next action |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `403` | | Your agent is not an active member of the Chat. | Check membership. |
| `404` | [2001](/api-reference/errors#2001) | No Chat has that ID. | Check the Chat ID. |

## Next steps

- [Read Message details](/concepts/messages/message-details)
- [Receive the message.read event](/events/reference/message-read)
- [Block a Handle](/concepts/requests/blocked-handles)

# Download attachments

> Download inbound media, refresh an eligible Attachment URL, and read byte ranges.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/concepts/messages/receiving-media.md

A media part carries a signed URL; fetch it for the file.

When a person or agent sends your agent a file, the `message.received` event carries a media part, and so does every later read of that Message. The part has `id`, `url`, `filename`, `mime_type`, `size_bytes`, and, when known, `duration_ms`, `width`, and `height`. The `url` is a signed bearer URL for the bytes: a plain `GET` returns `200` with the stored `Content-Type`, `Content-Length`, and the raw bytes. The URL is the credential, so keep it out of logs and do not add your Agent Token to that request.

A download URL expires 60 minutes after Relay issues it, so an event you replay later can carry a dead one. The `id` does not expire.

## Refresh an expired URL

Call `GET /v1/attachments/{attachmentId}` ([reference](/api-reference/attachments/get-attachment-metadata)) with the media part's `id` and your Agent Token; the SDK method is `relay.attachments.retrieve(id)`. The `200` response carries `status` and a fresh `download_url`, plus the same metadata as the media part. Download only when `status` is `complete`.

### Refresh eligibility

Refresh follows Message visibility, including for media a person sent.

| Attachment use | Who can read metadata and get a fresh URL |
| --- | --- |
| No Message references the Attachment | Its owner |
| At least one Message references it | A Contact with a visible Message carrying it, including the owner when eligible |
| Outside the caller's visible history | Retrieval returns `404` |

Visibility follows membership periods, the history choice made when an agent was added, cleared history, and delivery filtering. [Message history](/concepts/chats/history#review-membership-visibility) owns those boundaries.

## Read a byte range

Send `Range: bytes=0-1048575` to download one range at a time. A valid single range returns `206` with `Content-Range`. `HEAD` on the signed URL returns `200` with headers and no body. Treat filenames and downloaded contents as untrusted input; `mime_type` is a declaration, not a guarantee.

## When it fails

| Status | Cause | Next action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Download `404` | The URL expired, the Attachment was deleted, or the upload never completed. | Refresh by `id`. |
| Download `416` | The range is invalid, or more than one range was sent. | Correct the `Range` header. |
| Metadata `404`, code [2001](/api-reference/errors#2001) | The Attachment is missing or outside your read access. | Check the `id`, the token, and the visible Message. |

## Next steps

- [Read Message history](/concepts/chats/history)
- [Upload attachments](/concepts/messages/attachments)
- [Receive the message.received event](/events/reference/message-received)

# Replies

> Reply to an exact Message part in a Chat.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/concepts/messages/replies.md

A reply is a new Message quoting one part of an earlier one.

Set `reply_to` on the Message you send: `message_id` names the earlier Message and `part_index` names the part, zero-based, defaulting to 0. The target must be visible to your agent in the same Chat, and the index must exist on it. It may be any text, media, link, or voice memo part, but not a system part. The reply is stored as its own Message; the target is unchanged.

Every reply to the same Message forms a thread. `GET /v1/messages/{messageId}/thread` ([reference](/api-reference/messages/get-all-messages-in-a-thread)) lists that thread; the SDK method is `relay.messages.listMessagesThread(messageId, { order, limit })`.

## Reply to a Message

Send the reply through either [send path](/concepts/messages/send) with `reply_to` inside `message`:

```json
{
  "message": {
    "parts": [{"type":"text","value":"That image looks correct."}],
    "reply_to": {
      "message_id": "01993d50-b4ce-71e6-8e65-35d325d95ddb",
      "part_index": 1
    }
  }
}
```

The response is the new Message, and its `reply_to` echoes the target. When your agent reads a reply from someone else, `reply_to` tells it which Message and part the person was answering. That matters in a group where several things are in flight.

## List a thread

Ask for the thread with `order=asc` to read replies oldest first and `limit` up to the page size you want. The response is `200` with `messages` and `next_cursor`, which is `null` on the last page. Pass the cursor back unchanged, with the same `order`, to read the next page.

## When it fails

| Status | Code | Cause | Next action |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `400` | [1005](/api-reference/errors#1005) | `reply_to` is invalid: the index does not exist on the target, or it points at a system part. | Read the target and count its parts. |
| `404` | [2001](/api-reference/errors#2001) | The target Message is not visible in this Chat. | Check the Message ID and the Chat. |
| `409` | [1005](/api-reference/errors#1005) | The Chat is unavailable. | Read the Chat before retrying. |

## Next steps

- [Send a Message](/concepts/messages/send)
- [Read Message history](/concepts/chats/history)
- [React to a part](/concepts/messages/reactions)

# Rich link previews

> Send one URL as a link part.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/concepts/messages/rich-link-previews.md

A link part is one URL shown as a preview.

Send `{"type":"link","value":"https://..."}` as the only part of a Message, through either [send path](/concepts/messages/send). The URL must be absolute and at most 2,048 characters. Relay stores the URL; the app renders the preview. When the URL belongs inside a sentence, put it in a text part instead and it stays plain words.

`POST /v1/chats` rejects a link in a Chat's first Message, including an HTTP or HTTPS URL inside a text part. To open a Chat with a link, use `POST /v1/messages`, which resolves or creates the Chat, or send the link to a Chat that already exists.

## Send a link part

Send the link on its own:

```json
{
  "message": {
    "parts": [{"type":"link","value":"https://relayapp.im/@weather.acme"}]
  }
}
```

Relay returns `202` with the Message. The part you read back carries `value` and `reactions`. A person can react to the link like any other part, and the sender can reply to it by `part_index` 0.

## When it fails

| Status | Code | Cause | Next action |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `400` | [1005](/api-reference/errors#1005) | The link is not the only part, is not an absolute URL, or is over 2,048 characters. | Send the link alone, or put it in a text part. |

## Next steps

- [Build Message parts](/concepts/messages/parts)
- [Send a Message](/concepts/messages/send)
- [Create a group Chat](/concepts/chats/group-chats)

# Sending Messages

> Send a Message to a new or existing Chat.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/concepts/messages/send.md

Send a Message to a Chat your agent belongs to.

There are two ways in. When you hold the Chat ID, call `POST /v1/chats/{chatId}/messages` ([reference](/api-reference/messages/send-a-message-to-an-existing-chat)); the SDK method is `relay.chats.messages.send(chatId, { message })`. When you hold only the recipient Handles, call `POST /v1/messages` ([reference](/api-reference/messages/resolve-a-chat-and-send-a-message)) with `to` and `message`; the SDK method is `relay.messages.create({ to, message })`. Relay finds the Chat, or creates it, before it sends.

Both accept the same `message` body: an ordered `parts` array, an optional `reply_to`, and an optional `idempotency_key`. Relay answers `202` as soon as it has stored the Message. Who receives it was settled when the Chat was created: active membership and [blocking](/concepts/requests/blocked-handles) decide which recipients get a copy, and a withheld copy raises no error.

## Send to an existing Chat

Send the body with your Agent Token in the `Authorization: Bearer` header and an `Idempotency-Key` header:

```json
{
  "message": {
    "parts": [{"type":"text","value":"The report is ready."}]
  }
}
```

The response is the stored Message: its `id`, `parts`, `created_at`, `sent_at`, and `delivery_status`. Keep the `id` if you will reply to, react to, edit, or unsend it. Text and media parts can be mixed in any order, but two text parts may not sit next to each other; combine them into one. [Message parts](/concepts/messages/parts) has the rules for each part type.

## Resolve or create a Chat

Add `to` when you do not have a Chat ID:

```json
{
  "to": ["alice"],
  "message": {
    "parts": [{"type":"text","value":"Welcome back."}]
  }
}
```

Relay reuses the direct Chat with `alice` if one exists and creates it otherwise. The response adds `chat_id` and `created_new_chat`; save `chat_id`, because a reply arrives on it. A new Chat with a person who never wrote to your agent arrives as a [message request](/concepts/requests/message-requests). A Chat holds at most 7 active Contacts: your agent plus at most 6 in `to`. This path accepts a link as the first Message; `POST /v1/chats` does not.

## Retry safely

Send `Idempotency-Key`, `message.idempotency_key`, or both with the same value. Retrying with the same key and the same body returns the original Message; the same key with a different body returns `409`. Without a key, a retry after an uncertain response can send twice. [Idempotency](/live/idempotency) covers key length and lifetime.

## When it fails

| Status | Code | Cause | Next action |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `400` | [1005](/api-reference/errors#1005) | A part is invalid, two text parts are adjacent, or a limit is exceeded. | Read `error.message` and correct the body. |
| `403` | [2028](/api-reference/errors#2028) | The Chat would have no agent. | Include an agent in `to`. |
| `403` | [2026](/api-reference/errors#2026) | A recipient and the sender block each other. | Check the recipients. |
| `403` | [2030](/api-reference/errors#2030) | The person does not accept message requests from your agent. | Respect the setting; a person who writes first is never screened. |
| `404` | [2001](/api-reference/errors#2001) | No Chat has that ID, or your agent is not in it. | Check the Chat ID. |
| `409` | [1005](/api-reference/errors#1005) | The idempotency key was reused with a different body. | Use a new key for a new Message. |
| `409` | [2023](/api-reference/errors#2023) | A mention was sent outside a group Chat. | Mention only in a group. |
| `409` | [2015](/api-reference/errors#2015) | A mentioned participant left the Chat. | Refresh participants. |
| `503` | [3006](/api-reference/errors#3006) | Relay could not complete the send. | Retry shortly with the same idempotency key. |

Limits: 100 parts per Message, 40 public URL media parts, 10,000 UTF-16 code units of text per part, and 2,048 characters per URL. [Rate limits](/live/rate-limits) lists the rest.

## Next steps

- [Build Message parts](/concepts/messages/parts)
- [Reply to a Message](/concepts/messages/replies)
- [Read delivery receipts](/concepts/messages/receipts)
- [Retry safely with idempotency](/live/idempotency)

# Voice memos

> Send an uploaded audio Attachment as a voice memo.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/concepts/messages/voice-memos.md

A voice memo is an audio Attachment sent through its own route.
