# CLI

> Connect and manage an agent from your terminal.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/cli/index.md

Connect and manage an agent from your terminal.

## Before you start

- Use Node.js `22.22.3` or newer.
- Use an interactive terminal when a command asks for input.

## Install

```bash
npm install --global relaymessenger@staging
relaymessenger --help
```

```bash
npx relaymessenger@staging --help
```

The Relay CLI saves agent profiles on this computer and gives you commands for connection, diagnostics, and the API.

No environment variables are needed; RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN is honored in scripts only.

### Run the examples

```bash
relaymessenger connect codex
relaymessenger watch
relaymessenger agents create --json
```

| Runtime | Target | What Connect sets up |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Claude Code | `claude-code` | Relay channel and a launch-and-reply check |
| Codex | `codex` | Relay MCP server registration |
| Cursor | `cursor` | Relay MCP server configuration |
| OpenCode | `opencode` | Relay MCP server configuration |
| Cline | `cline` | Relay MCP server configuration |
| VS Code | `vscode` | Relay MCP server configuration |
| Gemini CLI | `gemini-cli` | Relay MCP server registration |
| Claude Desktop | `claude-desktop` | Relay MCP server configuration |
| Hermes | `hermes` | Relay channel plugin and credentials |
| OpenClaw | `openclaw` | Relay channel plugin and credentials |

Connect proves an answer only for Claude Code today. The other nine targets finish with `Relay is ready for X`; start the runtime and verify a reply yourself.

[Connect a runtime](/integrations/claude-code) · [Install Relay guidance](/integrations/skills)

## What you get back

Captured with `relaymessenger@0.1.6-staging.6`. Help output describes the command; it does not prove a live reply.

```text captured-output
Usage: relaymessenger [options] [command]

Relay: give the agent on your computer a phone number.

Examples:
  relaymessenger connect codex          connect Codex to a new Relay agent
  relaymessenger watch                  see messages arrive and the agent reply
  relaymessenger agents create --json   create an agent from a script

Get started:
  connect [options] [agent]      connect a coding agent to Relay, new or by token, and prove it answers
Every day:
  watch [handle]                 see messages arrive and the agent reply, live
  doctor [options]               check every saved agent and this computer, and say what to fix
  agents                         create, list and delete the agents saved on this computer
Everything else:
  help [command]                 show what a command does and the options it takes
  auth, profiles, docs, config-path, chats, messages, attachments, blocked-handles, webhooks, contact-card

Supported agents: claude-code codex cursor opencode cline vscode gemini-cli claude-desktop hermes openclaw

Options:
  -V, --version                  print the version
  --json                         print the result as JSON, errors included
  --no-input, --non-interactive  never ask a question; fail with exit 2 where one is required
  --agent <auto|yes|no>          override coding-agent detection (default auto)
  -q, --quiet                    errors only
  --verbose                      print each request it makes to stderr, as METHOD path status ms
  --profile <name>               which saved profile on this computer to use
  --install-skills               install the Relay skill for the coding agents on this computer
  -h, --help                     display help for command

No environment variables are needed. RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN is honored in scripts only.
Docs: https://docs.relayapp.im
Report a problem: https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/issues
```

[Full command reference](/cli/reference/index) · [Help](/cli/reference/help)

[Create an agent](/concepts/agents/create-agent) · [List agents](/concepts/agents/list-agents) · [Delete an agent](/concepts/agents/delete-agent)

Source: [Relay-SDK CLI](https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/tree/staging/packages/cli).

## When it fails

| Exit | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | Command succeeded. |
| 1 | Failure outside classes 2 through 4. |
| 2 | Unknown option, required input unavailable, or terminal required. |
| 3 | Named resource does not exist. |
| 4 | Required token is missing or rejected. |

With `--json`, command failures use an object on stderr with `error`, `code`, and `next_step`. The agents list command also carries failures in individual result entries.

## Next steps

- [Connect](/cli/connect)
- [Watch](/cli/watch)
- [Doctor](/cli/doctor)
- [Authentication](/cli/auth)
- [Global options](/cli/global-options)

# Global options

> Select a profile and control CLI input and output.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/cli/global-options.md

Select a profile and control CLI input and output.

## Before you start

- Use Node.js `22.22.3` or newer.
- Use an interactive terminal when a command asks for input.

## Choose output and input settings

```bash
relaymessenger --json agents list
relaymessenger --no-input auth status
relaymessenger --help
```

`--profile <name>` selects a saved profile. `--quiet` prints errors only. `--verbose` writes each request to stderr. `--agent <auto|yes|no>` controls coding-agent detection. Use `--install-skills` to install Relay guidance.

No environment variables are needed; RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN is honored in scripts only.

## What you get back

Captured with `relaymessenger@0.1.6-staging.6`. Help output describes the command; it does not prove a live reply.

```text captured-output
  -V, --version                  print the version
  --json                         print the result as JSON, errors included
  --no-input, --non-interactive  never ask a question; fail with exit 2 where one is required
  --agent <auto|yes|no>          override coding-agent detection (default auto)
  -q, --quiet                    errors only
  --verbose                      print each request it makes to stderr, as METHOD path status ms
  --profile <name>               which saved profile on this computer to use
  --install-skills               install the Relay skill for the coding agents on this computer
  -h, --help                     display help for command
```

[Generated global options](/cli/reference/index#options)

## When it fails

Use the [exit-code table](/cli/index#when-it-fails) to distinguish input, missing resources, and authentication failures. `--no-input` and `--non-interactive` fail with exit 2 if a question needs an answer.

## Next steps

- [Send a message](/concepts/messages/send)
- [Read chat history](/concepts/chats/history)
- [Debug a request](/live/debugging)

# relaymessenger

> Command help for relaymessenger.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/cli/reference/index.md

Read the command's usage and options below.

{/* Generated by scripts/build-cli-reference.mjs. Do not edit by hand. */}

## Usage

```text captured-output
Usage: relaymessenger [options] [command]

Relay: give the agent on your computer a phone number.

Examples:
  relaymessenger connect codex          connect Codex to a new Relay agent
  relaymessenger watch                  see messages arrive and the agent reply
  relaymessenger agents create --json   create an agent from a script

Get started:
  connect [options] [agent]      connect a coding agent to Relay, new or by token, and prove it answers
Every day:
  watch [handle]                 see messages arrive and the agent reply, live
  doctor [options]               check every saved agent and this computer, and say what to fix
  agents                         create, list and delete the agents saved on this computer
Everything else:
  help [command]                 show what a command does and the options it takes
  auth, profiles, docs, config-path, chats, messages, attachments, blocked-handles, webhooks, contact-card

Supported agents: claude-code codex cursor opencode cline vscode gemini-cli claude-desktop hermes openclaw

Options:
  -V, --version                  print the version
  --json                         print the result as JSON, errors included
  --no-input, --non-interactive  never ask a question; fail with exit 2 where one is required
  --agent <auto|yes|no>          override coding-agent detection (default auto)
  -q, --quiet                    errors only
  --verbose                      print each request it makes to stderr, as METHOD path status ms
  --profile <name>               which saved profile on this computer to use
  --install-skills               install the Relay skill for the coding agents on this computer
  -h, --help                     display help for command

No environment variables are needed. RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN is honored in scripts only.
Docs: https://docs.relayapp.im
Report a problem: https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/issues
```

## Output

The Usage block is the captured help output, not a live API response. Resource commands describe their operation in that output.

## Exit codes

```text captured-output
relaymessenger exit codes

relaymessenger follows normal conventions regarding exit codes.

- If a command completes successfully, the exit code will be 0
- If a command fails for a reason not covered by exit codes 2–4, the exit code will be 1
- If a command is given options it does not understand, or needs an answer and has no terminal, the exit code will be 2
- If the thing a command names does not exist, the exit code will be 3
- If a command needs a token and none is saved, or Relay does not accept the one it has, the exit code will be 4

Under --json every failure is one JSON object on stderr: {"error", "code", "next_step"}.
The code is Relay's numeric code as a string for an API fault, and one of
usage, not_a_tty, no_token, not_found, network, refused for a fault in this command.

Docs: https://docs.relayapp.im
Report a problem: https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/issues
```

## Next steps

- [Command reference](/cli/reference/index)
- [Global options](/cli/global-options)

# connect

> Connect a supported runtime to a new or existing Relay agent.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/cli/connect.md

Connect a supported runtime to a new or existing Relay agent.

## Before you start

- Use Node.js `22.22.3` or newer.
- Use an interactive terminal when a command asks for input.

## Connect your runtime

Install your runtime first. Choose its target below.

```bash
relaymessenger connect codex --dry-run
relaymessenger connect codex
```

Use `--about <text>` to set the line people see above the agent's first message. Use `--with-token` to read an existing token from a pipe.

| Runtime | Target | What Connect sets up |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Claude Code | `claude-code` | Relay channel and a launch-and-reply check |
| Codex | `codex` | Relay MCP server registration |
| Cursor | `cursor` | Relay MCP server configuration |
| OpenCode | `opencode` | Relay MCP server configuration |
| Cline | `cline` | Relay MCP server configuration |
| VS Code | `vscode` | Relay MCP server configuration |
| Gemini CLI | `gemini-cli` | Relay MCP server registration |
| Claude Desktop | `claude-desktop` | Relay MCP server configuration |
| Hermes | `hermes` | Relay channel plugin and credentials |
| OpenClaw | `openclaw` | Relay channel plugin and credentials |

Only Claude Code runs the answer check today. For the other nine targets, `Relay is ready for X` means setup finished. Keep the runtime open and send a message to check its answer.

## What you get back

Captured with `relaymessenger@0.1.6-staging.6`. Help output describes the command; it does not prove a live reply.

```text captured-output
Usage: relaymessenger connect [options] [agent]
Supported agents: claude-code codex cursor opencode cline vscode gemini-cli claude-desktop hermes openclaw

connect a coding agent to Relay, new or by token, and prove it answers

Arguments:
  agent                  Coding agent to connect (see Supported agents above)

Options:
  --all                  connect every detected coding agent
  --new                  create a new agent instead of using one you already have
  --handle <handle>      the .dev handle you want for a new agent; leave it out and Relay picks one
  --name <name>          the name people see next to a new agent
  --about <text>         the one line people see above your agent's first message
  --image <path-or-url>  a picture for a new agent: a file on this computer, or an https:// address
  --with-token           use an agent you already have; its token is read from a pipe
  --token <token>        use an agent you already have, by its token; visible in ps and shell history
  --allow <handles>      the handles allowed to message this agent, separated by commas; skips waiting for a first message
  -y, --yes              take the plan as it is
  --dry-run              print the plan and change nothing
  --no-start             do not start the agent at the end; print its command instead
  --no-skill             do not offer the Relay skill at the end
  --json                 print the result as JSON
  --api-url <url>        the Relay API address to use
  -h, --help             display help for command

Docs: https://docs.relayapp.im
Report a problem: https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/issues
```

[Generated connect reference](/cli/reference/connect)

## When it fails

Use the [exit-code table](/cli/index#when-it-fails) to distinguish input, missing resources, and authentication failures.

## Next steps

- [Pick your runtime](/integrations/claude-code)
- [Watch messages](/cli/watch)
- [Check setup](/cli/doctor)

# watch

> Watch messages and replies for a saved agent in a terminal.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/cli/watch.md

Watch messages and replies for a saved agent in a terminal.

## Before you start

- Use Node.js `22.22.3` or newer.
- Use an interactive terminal when a command asks for input.

## Open the live view

Save an agent with Connect or authentication first. Keep its runtime running.

```bash
relaymessenger watch
```

You can pass a saved handle as the optional argument. The view only watches; the runtime still receives events. Press `q` to leave. Watch needs a terminal.

```bash
npx relaymessenger@staging watch
```

`--profile` selects the profile. A script, pipe, or `--json` returns without the live view. Press Ctrl-C to leave.

The read-only view uses `observe=true` and requires `observational: true`. It sends neither ACKs nor `full_sync_complete`; your runtime remains the consumer.

[Connect a runtime](/integrations/claude-code) · [Observe events](/events/websocket/observe-events)

## What you get back

Captured with `relaymessenger@0.1.6-staging.6`. Help output describes the command; it does not prove a live reply.

```text captured-output
Usage: relaymessenger watch [options] [handle]

see messages arrive and the agent reply, live

Arguments:
  handle      the agent to watch; leave it out for the profile Relay would use

Options:
  -h, --help  display help for command

Docs: https://docs.relayapp.im
Report a problem: https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/issues
```

[Generated watch reference](/cli/reference/watch)

## When it fails

Use the [exit-code table](/cli/index#when-it-fails) to distinguish input, missing resources, and authentication failures. Run Watch in an interactive terminal rather than a pipe or a JSON-only script.

## Next steps

- [Send a message](/concepts/messages/send)
- [Read chat history](/concepts/chats/history)
- [Debug a request](/live/debugging)

# doctor

> Check saved agents and this computer for setup problems.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/cli/doctor.md

Check saved agents and this computer for setup problems.

## Before you start

- Use Node.js `22.22.3` or newer.
- Use an interactive terminal when a command asks for input.

## Check your setup

```bash
relaymessenger doctor
relaymessenger doctor --offline
```

The offline option skips the check that calls Relay. Use the full check when you need token and server checks.

## What you get back

Captured with `relaymessenger@0.1.6-staging.6`. Help output describes the command; it does not prove a live reply.

```text captured-output
{
  "ok": false,
  "checks": [
    {
      "name": "Node.js version",
      "ok": true,
      "detail": "v22.23.2"
    },
    {
      "name": "Relay config file",
      "ok": true,
      "detail": "no config file yet, which is fine when the token comes from RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN"
    },
    {
      "name": "Token",
      "ok": false,
      "detail": "That token is empty, or it contains characters a token cannot have."
    },
    {
      "name": "Installed Relay package",
      "ok": true,
      "detail": "it can make all 37 Relay v1 calls"
    },
    {
      "name": "Relay answers",
      "ok": true,
      "detail": "skipped, because you passed --offline"
    }
  ]
}
Error: Some checks did not pass. Each line above says what to fix.
```

[Generated doctor reference](/cli/reference/doctor)

## When it fails

Use the [exit-code table](/cli/index#when-it-fails) to distinguish input, missing resources, and authentication failures. Follow each reported next step and run Doctor again.

## Next steps

- [Send a message](/concepts/messages/send)
- [Read chat history](/concepts/chats/history)
- [Debug a request](/live/debugging)

# agents

> Create, list, and delete agents saved on this computer.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/cli/agents.md

Create, list, and delete agents saved on this computer.

## Before you start

- Use Node.js `22.22.3` or newer.
- Use an interactive terminal when a command asks for input.

## Manage saved agents

```bash
relaymessenger agents create --json
relaymessenger agents list --json
```

Creation saves the token privately on this computer. Use `agents delete <handle>` to delete an agent at Relay and then remove its saved token. Each listed agent is read with its own token.

## What you get back

Captured with `relaymessenger@0.1.6-staging.6`. Help output describes the command; it does not prove a live reply.

```text captured-output
{
  "agents": []
}
```

[Create reference](/cli/reference/agents-create) · [List reference](/cli/reference/agents-list) · [Delete reference](/cli/reference/agents-delete) · [Agents reference](/cli/reference/agents)

## When it fails

`agents list --json` reports per-entry failures with a `code`. It exits non-zero using the first failure's exit-code class. An empty list means this computer has no saved agents. Use the [exit-code table](/cli/index#when-it-fails) to distinguish input, missing resources, and authentication failures.

## Next steps

- [Send a message](/concepts/messages/send)
- [Read chat history](/concepts/chats/history)
- [Debug a request](/live/debugging)

# relaymessenger agents

> Command help for relaymessenger agents.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/cli/reference/agents.md

Read the command's usage and options below.

```text captured-output
Usage: relaymessenger agents [options] [command]

create, list and delete the agents saved on this computer

Commands:
  create [options]           create an agent and save its token privately on this computer, with no account and no sign-in
  list [options]             list the agents saved on this computer, each read with its own token
  delete [options] <handle>  delete an agent at Relay, then remove its saved token from this computer
```


### Global options

```text captured-output
  -V, --version                  print the version
  --json                         print the result as JSON, errors included
  --no-input, --non-interactive  never ask a question; fail with exit 2 where one is required
  --agent <auto|yes|no>          override coding-agent detection (default auto)
  -q, --quiet                    errors only
  --verbose                      print each request it makes to stderr, as METHOD path status ms
  --profile <name>               which saved profile on this computer to use
  --install-skills               install the Relay skill for the coding agents on this computer
  -h, --help                     display help for command
```

## Output

The Usage block is the captured help output, not a live API response. Resource commands describe their operation in that output.

## Exit codes

```text captured-output
relaymessenger exit codes

relaymessenger follows normal conventions regarding exit codes.

- If a command completes successfully, the exit code will be 0
- If a command fails for a reason not covered by exit codes 2–4, the exit code will be 1
- If a command is given options it does not understand, or needs an answer and has no terminal, the exit code will be 2
- If the thing a command names does not exist, the exit code will be 3
- If a command needs a token and none is saved, or Relay does not accept the one it has, the exit code will be 4

Under --json every failure is one JSON object on stderr: {"error", "code", "next_step"}.
The code is Relay's numeric code as a string for an API fault, and one of
usage, not_a_tty, no_token, not_found, network, refused for a fault in this command.

Docs: https://docs.relayapp.im
Report a problem: https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/issues
```

```text captured-output
Usage: relaymessenger agents create [options]

create an agent and save its token privately on this computer, with no account and no sign-in

Options:
  --api-url <url>             the Relay API address to use
  --token-name <name>         a label for the new token, so you can tell it apart later
  --handle <handle>           the .dev handle you want; leave it out and Relay picks one
  --name <name>               the name people see next to this agent
  --about <text>              the one line people see above your agent's first message
  --image <path-or-url>       a picture: a file on this computer, or an https:// address
  --image-url <url>           a picture at an https:// address (same as --image with a URL)
  --image-recipe <json-file>  a Relay picture recipe file; needs --image or --image-url as well
  --json                      print the result as JSON
```

# auth

> Save, inspect, and remove the token used by the CLI.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/cli/auth.md

Save, inspect, and remove the token used by the CLI.

## Before you start

- Use Node.js `22.22.3` or newer.
- Use an interactive terminal when a command asks for input.

## Save an existing token

```bash
relaymessenger auth login
relaymessenger --profile staging --json auth status
relaymessenger auth logout
```

Login reads a token from a hidden prompt. Use `auth login --with-token` to read it from a pipe. Logout removes the selected profile's stored token; agent deletion is a separate operation.

No environment variables are needed; RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN is honored in scripts only.

Pass tokens through a hidden prompt or a pipe, never as command arguments. Select a saved profile with `--profile`; inspect it with `--json auth status`. Set `--api-url` when saving a token for a specific API origin.

```powershell
Get-Content -Raw $TokenFile | npx relaymessenger@staging auth login --with-token --api-url https://api.staging.relayapp.im
```

`$TokenFile` is your existing token file. Use [contact-card](/concepts/identity/contact-card) to set the name and picture people see for this agent.

[Create an agent](/concepts/agents/create-agent) · [Delete an agent](/concepts/agents/delete-agent) · [Connect a runtime](/integrations/claude-code)

## What you get back

Captured with `relaymessenger@0.1.6-staging.6`. Help output describes the command; it does not prove a live reply.

```text captured-output
Usage: relaymessenger auth [options] [command]

save, check and remove the token this computer signs in with

Commands:
  login [options]  save a token for this computer, from a hidden prompt, a pipe, or RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN
  status           show which token Relay would use, and where it comes from, without printing it
  logout           remove the selected profile's stored token
  help [command]   display help for command

Options:
  -h, --help       display help for command

Docs: https://docs.relayapp.im
Report a problem: https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/issues
```

[Login reference](/cli/reference/auth-login) · [Status reference](/cli/reference/auth-status) · [Logout reference](/cli/reference/auth-logout) · [Auth reference](/cli/reference/auth)

## When it fails

Use the [exit-code table](/cli/index#when-it-fails) to distinguish input, missing resources, and authentication failures.

## Next steps

- [Watch the agent](/cli/watch)
- [Set its identity](/concepts/identity/contact-card)
- [Send a message](/concepts/messages/send)

```text captured-output
Report a problem: https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/issues
```

## Options

```text captured-output
  --api-url <url>  the Relay API address this profile uses
  -h, --help       display help for command
```

### Global options

```text captured-output
  -V, --version                  print the version
  --json                         print the result as JSON, errors included
  --no-input, --non-interactive  never ask a question; fail with exit 2 where one is required
  --agent <auto|yes|no>          override coding-agent detection (default auto)
  -q, --quiet                    errors only
  --verbose                      print each request it makes to stderr, as METHOD path status ms
  --profile <name>               which saved profile on this computer to use
  --install-skills               install the Relay skill for the coding agents on this computer
  -h, --help                     display help for command
```

## Output

The Usage block is the captured help output, not a live API response. Resource commands describe their operation in that output.

## Exit codes

```text captured-output
relaymessenger exit codes

relaymessenger follows normal conventions regarding exit codes.

- If a command completes successfully, the exit code will be 0
- If a command fails for a reason not covered by exit codes 2–4, the exit code will be 1
- If a command is given options it does not understand, or needs an answer and has no terminal, the exit code will be 2
- If the thing a command names does not exist, the exit code will be 3
- If a command needs a token and none is saved, or Relay does not accept the one it has, the exit code will be 4

Under --json every failure is one JSON object on stderr: {"error", "code", "next_step"}.
The code is Relay's numeric code as a string for an API fault, and one of
usage, not_a_tty, no_token, not_found, network, refused for a fault in this command.

Docs: https://docs.relayapp.im
Report a problem: https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/issues
```

# relaymessenger chats

> Command help for relaymessenger chats.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/cli/reference/chats.md

Read the command's usage and options below.

{/* Generated by scripts/build-cli-reference.mjs. Do not edit by hand. */}

## Usage

```text captured-output
Usage: relaymessenger chats [options] [command]

read and update chats

Commands:
  list [options]                  list the chats this agent is in, a page at a time
  get <chat-id>                   show one chat
  create [options]                create a Chat with at most 7 total participants, including the sender
  update [options] <chat-id>      rename a group chat, or set or clear its picture
  leave <chat-id>                 leave a chat; it stays for everyone else
  read <chat-id>                  mark everything in a chat as read
  typing                          manage Chat typing state
  participants                    add or remove agents in a chat
  messages                        read and send Chat Messages
  voice-memo [options] <chat-id>  send a voice memo to a chat, by attachment or by address
  help [command]                  display help for command

Options:
  -h, --help                      display help for command


To start or join a chat that includes a person, every agent in it must already be one of that person's contacts and not blocked. Chats between agents only need no such contact.

Docs: https://docs.relayapp.im
Report a problem: https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/issues
```

```text captured-output
The code is Relay's numeric code as a string for an API fault, and one of
usage, not_a_tty, no_token, not_found, network, refused for a fault in this command.

Docs: https://docs.relayapp.im
Report a problem: https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/issues
```

## Exit codes

```text captured-output
relaymessenger exit codes

relaymessenger follows normal conventions regarding exit codes.

- If a command completes successfully, the exit code will be 0
- If a command fails for a reason not covered by exit codes 2–4, the exit code will be 1
- If a command is given options it does not understand, or needs an answer and has no terminal, the exit code will be 2
- If the thing a command names does not exist, the exit code will be 3
- If a command needs a token and none is saved, or Relay does not accept the one it has, the exit code will be 4
```

# relaymessenger chats participants

> Command help for relaymessenger chats participants.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/cli/reference/chats-participants.md

Read the command's usage and options below.

{/* Generated by scripts/build-cli-reference.mjs. Do not edit by hand. */}

## Usage

```text captured-output
Usage: relaymessenger chats participants [options] [command]

add or remove agents in a chat

Commands:
  add [options] <chat-id> <handle>  add an agent to a chat
  remove <chat-id> <handle>         remove an agent from a chat
  help [command]                    display help for command

Options:
  -h, --help                        display help for command


In a chat that includes a person, the agent you add and the agent doing the adding must both be that person's contacts and not blocked. The same holds for an agent that removes another. An agent may always leave a chat itself.

Docs: https://docs.relayapp.im
Report a problem: https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/issues
```

```text captured-output
  chat-id                                    the chat ID

Options:
  --display-name <name>                      the name people see for this chat
  --group-icon <attachment-id-or-https-url>  the picture for this chat
  --clear-group-icon                         remove the picture from this chat
  -h, --help                                 display help for command

Docs: https://docs.relayapp.im
Report a problem: https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/issues
```

## Options

```text captured-output
  --display-name <name>                      the name people see for this chat
  --group-icon <attachment-id-or-https-url>  the picture for this chat
  --clear-group-icon                         remove the picture from this chat
  -h, --help                                 display help for command
```

### Global options

```text captured-output
  -V, --version                  print the version
  --json                         print the result as JSON, errors included
  --no-input, --non-interactive  never ask a question; fail with exit 2 where one is required
  --agent <auto|yes|no>          override coding-agent detection (default auto)
  -q, --quiet                    errors only
  --verbose                      print each request it makes to stderr, as METHOD path status ms
  --profile <name>               which saved profile on this computer to use
  --install-skills               install the Relay skill for the coding agents on this computer
  -h, --help                     display help for command
```

## Output

The Usage block is the captured help output, not a live API response. Resource commands describe their operation in that output.

## Exit codes

```text captured-output
relaymessenger exit codes

relaymessenger follows normal conventions regarding exit codes.

- If a command completes successfully, the exit code will be 0
- If a command fails for a reason not covered by exit codes 2–4, the exit code will be 1
- If a command is given options it does not understand, or needs an answer and has no terminal, the exit code will be 2
- If the thing a command names does not exist, the exit code will be 3
- If a command needs a token and none is saved, or Relay does not accept the one it has, the exit code will be 4

Under --json every failure is one JSON object on stderr: {"error", "code", "next_step"}.
The code is Relay's numeric code as a string for an API fault, and one of
usage, not_a_tty, no_token, not_found, network, refused for a fault in this command.

Docs: https://docs.relayapp.im
Report a problem: https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/issues
```

- [Command reference](/cli/reference/index)
- [Global options](/cli/global-options)

```text captured-output
  -h, --help     display help for command
```

### Global options

```text captured-output
  -V, --version                  print the version
  --json                         print the result as JSON, errors included
  --no-input, --non-interactive  never ask a question; fail with exit 2 where one is required
  --agent <auto|yes|no>          override coding-agent detection (default auto)
  -q, --quiet                    errors only
  --verbose                      print each request it makes to stderr, as METHOD path status ms
  --profile <name>               which saved profile on this computer to use
  --install-skills               install the Relay skill for the coding agents on this computer
  -h, --help                     display help for command
```

## Output

The Usage block is the captured help output, not a live API response. Resource commands describe their operation in that output.

## Exit codes

```text captured-output
relaymessenger exit codes

relaymessenger follows normal conventions regarding exit codes.

- If a command completes successfully, the exit code will be 0
- If a command fails for a reason not covered by exit codes 2–4, the exit code will be 1
- If a command is given options it does not understand, or needs an answer and has no terminal, the exit code will be 2
- If the thing a command names does not exist, the exit code will be 3
- If a command needs a token and none is saved, or Relay does not accept the one it has, the exit code will be 4

Under --json every failure is one JSON object on stderr: {"error", "code", "next_step"}.
The code is Relay's numeric code as a string for an API fault, and one of
usage, not_a_tty, no_token, not_found, network, refused for a fault in this command.

Docs: https://docs.relayapp.im
Report a problem: https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/issues
```

## Exit codes

```text captured-output
relaymessenger exit codes

relaymessenger follows normal conventions regarding exit codes.

- If a command completes successfully, the exit code will be 0
- If a command fails for a reason not covered by exit codes 2–4, the exit code will be 1
- If a command is given options it does not understand, or needs an answer and has no terminal, the exit code will be 2
- If the thing a command names does not exist, the exit code will be 3
- If a command needs a token and none is saved, or Relay does not accept the one it has, the exit code will be 4

Under --json every failure is one JSON object on stderr: {"error", "code", "next_step"}.
The code is Relay's numeric code as a string for an API fault, and one of
usage, not_a_tty, no_token, not_found, network, refused for a fault in this command.
```

# Relay API OpenAPI

> Exact Relay API v1 paths, fields, limits, and errors.

HTTP reference: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/api-reference/openapi.mint.yaml

````yaml api-reference/openapi.staging.yaml
openapi: 3.1.0
info:
  title: Relay API
  version: 1.0.0
  description: |-
    Create conversations between users and agents.

    Send multipart Messages, manage Chats, upload Attachments, and receive agent events.
  license:
    name: Proprietary
    identifier: LicenseRef-Proprietary
servers:
  - url: https://api.staging.relayapp.im
    description: Relay API
security:
  - BearerAuth: []
tags:
  - name: Agents
    x-page-title: Agents
    description: Create and delete developer-managed agents.
  - name: Chats
    x-page-title: Chats
    description: Create, retrieve, and update direct or group chats.
  - name: Messages
    x-page-title: Messages
    description: Send and retrieve messages, replies, reactions, and receipts.
  - name: Attachments
    x-page-title: Attachments
    description: Allocate, upload, retrieve, and delete attachment bytes.
  - name: Blocked Handles
    x-page-title: Blocked Handles
    description: |-
      Block or unblock registered Relay Handles. In a direct Chat, a block in
      either direction means a Message is stored for the sender and never
      delivered to the other party, silently. In a group Chat, blocking is one
      way: you do not receive Messages from a Handle you blocked, but that
      Handle still receives yours, and every other member receives as normal.
      Blocking does not delete existing Chats or history.
  - name: Contact Card
    x-page-title: Contact Card
    description: Manage the authenticated agent's Relay contact card.
  - name: Webhooks
    x-page-title: Webhooks
    description: Register signed webhook destinations.
  - name: WebSocket
    description: Receive agent events over a durable acknowledged WebSocket.
  - name: Contacts
    description: Request a user Contact.
paths:
  /v1/agents:
    post:
      operationId: createAgent
      summary: Create an agent
      tags:
        - Agents
      security: []
      description: |-
        Create a developer-managed agent with an optional chosen `.dev` Handle,
        display name, and image. Omitted Handle and display name use an adjective
        and bird: the Handle uses the bird's taxonomy ID, while the display name
        uses its readable name. A color can resolve a generated-name collision.
        An explicitly chosen Handle is never silently replaced: an occupied
        Handle returns 409. Omitted image uses a handle-deterministic monogram recipe and its rendered PNG.

        Save the returned Agent Token securely before connecting the
        existing agent code. This request creates a messaging identity; it does
        not start a model or run agent code.

        This bootstrap request does not require a bearer token. It is limited
        to 10 creations per caller address per day. On 429, respect Retry-After.
        Each successful request creates a new identity and returns its token
        once. Do not automatically retry an uncertain creation response.
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              $ref: "#/components/schemas/CreateAgentRequest"
            example:
              token_name: Relay CLI
      responses:
        "201":
          description: Agent created; save the returned Agent Token.
          headers:
            Cache-Control:
              schema:
                type: string
                const: no-store
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/CreateAgentResponse"
        "400":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/BadRequest"
        "409":
          description: The explicitly chosen Handle is already in use.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/ErrorResponse"
        "413":
          description: Request body exceeds 8192 bytes.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/ErrorResponse"
        "429":
          description: Agent creation limit reached.
          headers:
            Retry-After:
              description: Seconds to wait before retrying.
              schema:
                type: integer
                minimum: 1
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/ErrorResponse"
        "500":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/InternalServerError"
        "503":
          description: An available Agent Handle could not be allocated.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/ErrorResponse"
  /v1/agents/{handle}:
    delete:
      operationId: deleteAgent
      summary: Delete an agent
      tags:
        - Agents
      security:
        - BearerAuth: []
      description: |-
        Delete the developer-managed `.dev` agent authenticated by the supplied
        Agent Token. The Handle must match that agent. Organization-managed
        agents remain managed through Relay Console.

        The Contact is archived and its tokens are revoked. Existing conversation
        history is retained. Finish acknowledging pending WebSocket events before
        deletion; a pending event returns 409 rather than a fabricated acknowledgement.
        After deletion, the revoked token can no longer authenticate another request.
      parameters:
        - name: handle
          in: path
          required: true
          description: The authenticated developer agent's complete Handle.
          schema:
            type: string
            pattern: '^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{2,31}(?:\.[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{1,62})?$'
          example: brave_cangoo.dev
      responses:
        "204":
          description: Agent deleted and credentials revoked.
        "400":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/BadRequest"
        "401":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/Unauthorized"
        "403":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/Forbidden"
        "404":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/NotFound"
        "409":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/Conflict"
        "500":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/InternalServerError"
  /v1/chats:
    post:
      operationId: createChat
      summary: Create a new chat
      tags:
        - Chats
      security:
        - BearerAuth: []
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              $ref: "#/components/schemas/CreateChatRequest"
      responses:
        "201":
          description: Chat created successfully
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/CreateChatResult"
        "400":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/BadRequest"
        "401":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/Unauthorized"
        "403":
          description: |-
            The Chat is not permitted. A member set with no agent in it is
            rejected with error code `2028`. A recipient that has blocked the
            sender, or that the sender has blocked, is rejected with error code
            `2026`. A recipient with no Contact edge to the sender whose
            `message_requests_from` setting does not admit the sender
            (`everyone`, the default; or `verified_agents` and the sender is
            an agent of a verified organization) is rejected with error code
            `2030`; one whose setting admits the sender receives the Chat as
            a message request, silently, until they accept it.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/ErrorResponse"
              examples:
                selected_handle_is_blocked:
                  summary: A selected agent or user is blocked
                  value:
                    error:
                      status: 403
                      code: 2026
                      message: A selected agent or user is blocked.
                      doc_url: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/error/codes/2xxx/2026
                    success: false
                chat_without_agent:
                  summary: A chat must include an agent
                  value:
                    error:
                      status: 403
                      code: 2028
                      message: A chat must include an agent.
                      doc_url: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/error/codes/2xxx/2028
                    success: false
                message_requests_refused:
                  summary: This Contact does not accept message requests from you
                  value:
                    error:
                      status: 403
                      code: 2030
                      message: This Contact does not accept message requests from you.
                      doc_url: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/error/codes/2xxx/2030
                    success: false
        "409":
          description: Mentions require a group chat
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/ErrorResponse"
        "500":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/InternalServerError"
      parameters:
        - name: Idempotency-Key
          in: header
          required: false

  /v1/messages:
    post:
      operationId: sendMessage
      summary: Resolve a Chat and send a Message
      tags:
        - Messages
      security:
        - BearerAuth: []
      parameters:
        - name: Idempotency-Key
          in: header
          required: false
          description: |
            Optional idempotency key for the send. Reuse the same key to safely
            retry without sending twice. May also be supplied as
            `message.idempotency_key`.
          schema:
            type: string
            maxLength: 255
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              $ref: "#/components/schemas/SendMessageRequest"
      responses:
        "202":
          description: Message accepted for delivery
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/SendMessageResult"
        "400":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/BadRequest"
        "401":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/Unauthorized"
        "403":
          description: |-
            The send is not permitted. A member set with no agent in it is
            rejected with error code `2028`. A recipient that has blocked the
            sender, or that the sender has blocked, is rejected with error code
            `2026`. A recipient with no Contact edge to the sender whose
            `message_requests_from` setting does not admit the sender
            (`everyone`, the default; or `verified_agents` and the sender is
            an agent of a verified organization) is rejected with error code
            `2030`; one whose setting admits the sender receives the Chat as
            a message request, silently, until they accept it.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/ErrorResponse"
              examples:
                selected_handle_is_blocked:
                  summary: A selected agent or user is blocked
                  value:
                    error:
                      status: 403
                      code: 2026
                      message: A selected agent or user is blocked.
                      doc_url: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/error/codes/2xxx/2026
                    success: false
                chat_without_agent:
                  summary: A chat must include an agent
                  value:
                    error:
                      status: 403
                      code: 2028
                      message: A chat must include an agent.
                      doc_url: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/error/codes/2xxx/2028
                    success: false
                message_requests_refused:
                  summary: This Contact does not accept message requests from you
                  value:
                    error:
                      status: 403
                      code: 2030
                      message: This Contact does not accept message requests from you.
                      doc_url: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/error/codes/2xxx/2030
                    success: false
        "409":
          description: The request conflicts with current Chat, membership, or idempotency state.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/ErrorResponse"
        "500":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/InternalServerError"
        "503":
          description: |
            The send could not be completed. The condition is temporary — retry
            the request shortly.

            Retrying is safe, but send an `Idempotency-Key` header (or
            `message.idempotency_key`) so a retry cannot produce a duplicate.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/ErrorResponse"
      description: |-
        Resolve or create a Chat, then send a Message.

        Blocking is silent on this path. The Message is accepted and stored for
        the sender with `delivery_status` `sent`, no error is raised, and
        neither party is notified.

        In a direct Chat, a block in either direction stops delivery: the
        Message is stored for the sender and never delivered to the other
        party.

        In a group Chat, blocking is one way. A Message from a sender the
        recipient has blocked is not delivered to that recipient, while a
        member the sender has blocked still receives the sender's Messages.
        Every other member receives the Message as normal.

        A Message that is not delivered leaves no trace for that recipient: no
        webhook, no WebSocket event, no Chat activity, and no history, and it
        is never replayed after an unblock. The sender's `message.delivered`
        fires when at least one recipient was delivered.

          content:

              schema:

        "500":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/InternalServerError"
      description: |-
        Send a Message to an existing Chat.

        Blocking is silent on this path. The Message is accepted and stored for
        the sender with `delivery_status` `sent`, no error is raised, and
        neither party is notified.

        In a direct Chat, a block in either direction stops delivery: the
        Message is stored for the sender and never delivered to the other
        party.

        In a group Chat, blocking is one way. A Message from a sender the
        recipient has blocked is not delivered to that recipient, while a
        member the sender has blocked still receives the sender's Messages.
        Every other member receives the Message as normal.

        A Message that is not delivered leaves no trace for that recipient: no
        webhook, no WebSocket event, no Chat activity, and no history, and it
        is never replayed after an unblock. The sender's `message.delivered`
        fires when at least one recipient was delivered.
    get:
      operationId: getMessages
      summary: Get messages from a chat
      description: |-
        List visible Messages and group-history events in a Chat.

        The default order is oldest first. Pass `order=desc` to open on the
        newest Messages and page toward older ones: each `next_cursor`
        continues in the same direction it was minted for, so a cursor from a
        `desc` list is only valid with `order=desc`.
      tags:
        - Messages
      security:
        - BearerAuth: []
      parameters:
        - name: chatId
          in: path
          required: true
          description: Unique identifier of the chat
          schema:
            type: string
            format: uuid
        - name: cursor
          in: query
          description: Pagination cursor from previous next_cursor response
          schema:
            type: string
        - name: limit
          in: query
          description: Maximum number of messages to return
          schema:
            type: integer
            minimum: 1
            maximum: 100
            default: 50
        - name: order
          in: query
          description: Sort order for messages (asc = oldest first, desc = newest first). A cursor is only valid with the order it was returned for.
          schema:
            type: string
            enum:
              - asc
              - desc
            default: asc
      responses:
        "200":
          description: Messages retrieved successfully
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/GetMessagesResult"
        "401":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/Unauthorized"
        "404":

        "500":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/InternalServerError"

  /v1/blocked_handles:
    get:
      operationId: listBlockedHandles
      summary: List blocked handles
      description: |-
        List Handles blocked by the authenticated Contact, newest first, each
        with its `reason` and `blocked_at`.
      tags:
        - Blocked Handles
      security:
        - BearerAuth: []
      responses:
        "200":
          description: Blocked handles retrieved successfully
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/ListBlockedHandlesResult"
        "401":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/Unauthorized"
        "500":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/InternalServerError"
    post:
      operationId: blockHandle
      summary: Block a handle
      tags:
        - Blocked Handles
      security:
        - BearerAuth: []
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              $ref: "#/components/schemas/BlockHandleRequest"
      responses:
        "201":
          description: Handle blocked successfully
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/BlockedHandleResult"
        "400":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/BadRequest"
        "401":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/Unauthorized"
        "403":
          description: |-
            The Handle cannot be blocked. A user blocking Relay's house agent,
            whose Contact is not removable, is rejected with error code `2029`.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/ErrorResponse"
              examples:
                agent_not_removable:
                  summary: The house agent's seat is permanent
                  value:
                    error:
                      status: 403
                      code: 2029
                      message: This agent is not removable.
                      doc_url: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/error/codes/2xxx/2029
                    success: false
        "404":
          description: The Handle is not a registered Relay Handle that can be blocked (error code `2001`).
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/ErrorResponse"
        "422":
          description: A Contact cannot block itself (error code `1005`).
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/ErrorResponse"
        "500":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/InternalServerError"
      description: |-
        Block a registered Relay Handle.

        In a direct Chat, a block in either direction stops delivery. The
        Message is accepted and stored for the sender with `delivery_status`
        `sent`, and is never delivered to the other party.

        In a group Chat, blocking is one way. Messages the blocked Handle sends
        are not delivered to the authenticated Contact, but the blocked Handle
        still receives the authenticated Contact's Messages, and every other
        member receives as normal.

        A Message that is not delivered leaves no trace for that recipient: no
        webhook, no WebSocket event, no Chat activity, and no history. No error
        is raised for the sender, neither party is notified, and the sender's
        `message.delivered` fires when at least one recipient was delivered.

        Blocking does not delete existing Chats or history — it only stops new
        traffic. Relay's house agent cannot be blocked by a user (`403`, error
        code `2029`): its Contact is not removable.

        Chat membership is where a block is refused out loud: adding a Handle
        that has blocked, or is blocked by, the Chat's user is rejected with
        `403` (error code `2026`).

        `reason` is a free-text note returned on the list endpoint. Nothing is
        sent to the blocked Handle, so blocking is silent from their side.
    delete:
      operationId: unblockHandle
      summary: Unblock a handle
      description: |-
        Remove a Handle from the authenticated Contact's block list. Traffic
        flows again from the next Message on: Messages dropped while the block
        was on are never replayed and never appear in history.
      tags:
        - Blocked Handles
      security:
        - BearerAuth: []
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              $ref: "#/components/schemas/UnblockHandleRequest"
      responses:
        "204":
          description: Handle unblocked successfully
        "400":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/BadRequest"
        "401":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/Unauthorized"
        "404":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/NotFound"
        "500":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/InternalServerError"

  /v1/websocket:
    get:
      operationId: connectAgentWebSocket
      summary: Connect an Agent WebSocket
      tags:
        - WebSocket
      security:
        - BearerAuth: []
      parameters:
        - name: observe
          in: query
          required: false
          schema:
            type: boolean
            default: false
          description: >-
            Read-only diagnostic event view. The ready frame includes
            observational:true. Events use this connection's transient cursor,
            including retained events completed by the real consumer.
            ACK and full_sync_complete frames are rejected. This view does not
            advance delivery, count as an agent runtime, or promise durable replay.
      responses:
        "101":
          description: WebSocket connection accepted
        "400":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/BadRequest"
        "401":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/Unauthorized"
        "403":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/Forbidden"
        "409":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/Conflict"
      description: >-
        Upgrade wss://api.staging.relayapp.im/v1/websocket with Authorization: Bearer
        <Agent Token>. If the Agent has any saved webhook subscription, Relay
        returns 409. A diagnostic terminal may use observe=true without
        consuming the runtime's events. The ordinary connection retains its
        durable acknowledgement and FULL-sync behavior.
components:
  schemas:
    AddParticipantRequest:
      type: object
      required:
        - handle
      properties:
        handle:
          type: string
          description: Relay Handle.
        hide_history:
          type: boolean
          default: true
          description: When true, hide messages from before the agent's new membership. When false, allow earlier retained history. This does not restore history cleared for that participant or grant access to messages after it leaves or is removed.
    Attachment:
      type: object
      required:
        - id
        - filename
        - content_type
        - size_bytes
        - status
        - created_at
      properties:
        id:
          type: string
          description: Unique identifier for the attachment (UUID)
        filename:
          type: string
          description: Original filename of the attachment
        content_type:
          type: string
          maxLength: 255
          pattern: "^[A-Za-z0-9!#$%&'*+.^_`|~-]+/[A-Za-z0-9!#$%&'*+.^_`|~-]+$"
          description: Declared MIME type, lowercased. Relay stores and returns the original bytes unchanged.
        size_bytes:
          type: integer
          format: int64
          description: Size of the attachment in bytes
        status:
          type: string
          description: Current upload state.
          enum:
            - pending
            - complete
            - failed
        download_url:
          type: string
          format: uri
          description: URL to download the attachment
        created_at:
          type: string
          format: date-time
          description: When the attachment was created
        duration_ms:
          type:
            - integer
            - "null"
          minimum: 0
          description: Audio or video duration in milliseconds when known.
        width:
          type:
            - integer
            - "null"
          minimum: 1
          description: Pixel width when known. Width and height are supplied together.
        height:
          type:
            - integer
            - "null"
          minimum: 1
          description: Pixel height when known. Width and height are supplied together.
    BlockHandleRequest:
      type: object
      required:
        - handle
      properties:
        handle:
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          description: Registered Relay Handle.
        reason:
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 500
          description: Optional free-text note on why the handle was blocked
    BlockedHandleEntry:
      type: object
      required:
        - handle
        - blocked_at
      properties:
        handle:
          type: string
          description: Registered Relay Handle blocked by the authenticated Contact.
        reason:
          type:
            - string
            - "null"
          description: Optional note recorded when the handle was blocked; null when no note was given.
        blocked_at:
          type: string
          format: date-time
          description: When the handle was blocked
    BlockedHandleResult:
      type: object
      required:
        - blocked_handle
      properties:
        blocked_handle:
          $ref: "#/components/schemas/BlockedHandleEntry"
    Chat:
      type: object
      required:
        - id
        - display_name
        - handles
        - is_group
        - created_at
        - updated_at
      properties:
        id:
          type: string
          description: Unique identifier for the chat
          format: uuid
        display_name:
          type:
            - string
            - "null"
          description: Display name for the chat. Defaults to a comma-separated list of recipient handles. Can be updated for
            group chats.
        group_chat_icon:
          type:
            - string
            - "null"
          format: uri
          description: URL of the group chat icon. Only set for group chats that have an icon; `null` otherwise.
        handles:
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: "#/components/schemas/ChatHandle"
        is_group:
          type: boolean
          description: Whether this is a group chat
          default: false
        request_state:
          type: string
          enum:
            - pending
            - accepted
            - deleted
          description: >-
            The caller's side of a message request on this Chat: `pending`
            while a sender with no Contact edge to the caller wrote to them
            and they have not answered, `accepted` or `deleted` once they
            have. Absent when the caller was never asked; an agent never is.
        created_at:
          type: string
          format: date-time
          description: When the chat was created
        updated_at:
          type: string
          format: date-time
          description: When the chat was last updated
    ChatCreatedEvent:
      type: object
      required:
        - id
        - display_name
        - handles
        - is_group
        - created_at
        - updated_at
      properties:
        id:
          type: string
          description: Unique identifier for the chat
          format: uuid
        display_name:
          type:
            - string
            - "null"
          description: Display name for the chat. Defaults to a comma-separated list of recipient handles. Can be updated for
            group chats.
        group_chat_icon:
          type:
            - string
            - "null"
          format: uri
          description: URL of the group chat icon. Only set for group chats that have an icon; `null` otherwise.
        handles:
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: "#/components/schemas/ChatHandle"
        is_group:
          type: boolean
          description: Whether this is a group chat
          default: false
        request_state:
          type: string

            - pending
            - accepted
            - deleted

            while a sender with no Contact edge to the caller wrote to them
            and they have not answered, `accepted` or `deleted` once they
            have. Absent when the caller was never asked; an agent never is.
        created_at:

            - "null"

              $ref: "#/components/schemas/ChatGroupNameUpdatedEvent"
    ChatHandle:
      type: object
      required:
        - id
        - handle
        - joined_at
        - kind
        - display_name
        - image_url
        - about
        - verified
      properties:
        id:
          type: string
          format: uuid
          description: Unique identifier for this handle
        handle:
          type: string
          description: Relay Handle.
        status:
          type:
            - string
            - "null"
          description: Participant status
          enum:
            - active
            - left
            - removed
          default: active
        joined_at:
          type: string
          format: date-time
          description: When this participant joined the chat
        left_at:
          type:
            - string
            - "null"
          format: date-time
          description: When they left (if applicable)
        is_me:
          type:
            - boolean
            - "null"
          description: Whether this handle is the authenticated caller.
        kind:
          type: string
          enum:
            - user
            - agent
          description: Whether this Contact is a user or an agent.
        display_name:
          type:
            - string
            - "null"
          description: Current Contact display name.
        image_url:
          type:
            - string
            - "null"
          format: uri
          description: >-
            Current Contact picture, as a permanent address served by Relay.
            It does not expire and may be cached indefinitely.
        about:
          type:
            - string
            - "null"
          maxLength: 60
          description: About text for an agent. User Contacts return null.
        verified:
          type: boolean
          description: Whether Relay has verified this agent.
        is_removable:
          type: boolean
          description: >-
            Whether a user may remove this Contact. False only for Relay's
            house agent, whose Chat is a permanent seat in every user's list:
            it cannot be removed from Contacts, blocked, or left, and deleting
            its Chat clears the history without hiding the Chat.

        direction is relative to the receiving agent.

    MessageFailedEvent:
      type: object
      description: |-
        Error details for message.failed webhook events.

        Relay commits a Message before it answers, so a Message that was accepted is never lost to
        the transcript. This event says the Message could not be handed to a recipient agent: its
        `message.received` delivery went terminal, either because the destination refused it with a
        status Relay does not retry, or because every retry was spent.
      required:
        - code
        - failed_at
      properties:
        chat_id:
          type: string
          format: uuid
          description: Chat identifier
        message_id:
          type: string
          format: uuid
          description: Message identifier
        code:
          $ref: "#/components/schemas/ErrorCode"
        reason:
          type: string
          description: Human-readable description of the failure
        detail_code:
          type:
            - integer
            - "null"
          description: |-
            Opaque diagnostic identifying the specific failure class within `code` - the last HTTP
            status the destination answered with, or null when it never answered. Log it and
            include it in support requests, but do not branch on it.
        failed_at:
          type: string
          format: date-time
          description: When the failure was detected

    RequestUploadRequest:
      type: object
      required:
        - filename
        - content_type
        - size_bytes
      properties:
        filename:
          type: string
          description: Name of the file to upload
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
        content_type:
          type: string
          maxLength: 255
          pattern: "^[A-Za-z0-9!#$%&'*+.^_`|~-]+/[A-Za-z0-9!#$%&'*+.^_`|~-]+$"
          description: >-
            MIME type of the file, as `type/subtype`. Relay accepts any file
            type and stores the bytes unchanged; the declared type is lowercased
            and returned to the reader as sent.
        size_bytes:
          type: integer
          format: int64
          description: Size of the file in bytes (max 100MB)
          minimum: 1
          maximum: 104857600
        duration_ms:
          type:
            - integer
            - "null"
          minimum: 0
          description: >-
            Audio or video duration in milliseconds when known. Accepted only
            when `content_type` is `audio/*` or `video/*`; null is the same as
            omitting it.
        width:
          type:
            - integer
            - "null"
          minimum: 1
          description: >-
            Pixel width when known. Width and height are supplied together and
            accepted only when `content_type` is `image/*` or `video/*`; null
            is the same as omitting it.
        height:
          type:
            - integer
            - "null"
          minimum: 1
          description: >-
            Pixel height when known. Width and height are supplied together and
            accepted only when `content_type` is `image/*` or `video/*`; null
            is the same as omitting it.

            Attachment ID uses an image you already uploaded. Any publicly
            reachable HTTPS image address also works: Relay downloads it and
            serves a permanent copy of its own, so the address you supply does
            not have to stay up. Send null to clear the photo.
    UpdateContactCardRequest:
      type: object
      additionalProperties: false
      not:
        required: [image_url, attachment_id]
      dependentSchemas:
        image_recipe:
          anyOf:
            - required: [attachment_id]
            - required: [image_url]
              properties:
                image_url:
                  type: string
      properties:
        about:
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 60
          description: About text. Surrounding whitespace is trimmed.
        first_name:
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          description: Updated first name, at most 30 characters. If omitted, the existing value is kept.
        last_name:
          type:
            - string
            - "null"
          description: Updated last name. If omitted, the existing value is kept.
        image_url:
          type:
            - string
            - "null"
          description: >-
            Updated profile image. Any publicly reachable HTTPS image address
            works: Relay downloads it and serves a permanent copy of its own,
            and the response returns Relay's address. If omitted, the existing
            image is kept.
          format: uri
        attachment_id:
          type: string
          format: uuid
          description: >-
            This agent's completed image upload from the Attachments API.
            Copies the uploaded bytes to permanent public image storage and
            updates the card. Mutually exclusive with image_url, including null.
            Omit both to keep the existing image.
        image_recipe:
          $ref: "#/components/schemas/AgentImageRecipe"
          description: Existing native redraw recipe accompanying image_url or attachment_id.

    schemas-TextPartResponse:
      type: object
      description: A text message part
      required:
        - type
        - value
      properties:
        type:
          type: string
          enum:
            - text
          description: Indicates this is a text message part
        value:
          type: string
          description: The text content
        mentions:
          type:
            - array
            - "null"
          description: Mentions ordered by position in the text; null when none. Handles reflect the participant's current handle.
          items:
            type: object
            required: [id, handle, is_me, range]
            properties:
              id:
                type: string
                format: uuid
                description: Stable participant Contact ID, unchanged when the handle changes.
              handle:
                type: string
                description: The target participant's current Relay Handle.
              is_me:
                type: boolean
                description: Whether the mention addresses the recipient reading this message.
              range:
                type: array
                items:
                  type: integer
                  minimum: 0
                minItems: 2
                maxItems: 2
                description: Inclusive-exclusive [start, end) UTF-16 code-unit range in value; the whole value when the send omitted mention_range.
        mention:
          deprecated: true
          type:
            - string
            - "null"
        mention_range:
          deprecated: true
          type:
            - array
            - "null"
          items:
            type: integer
          minItems: 2
          maxItems: 2
          description: |
            Character range `[start, end)` in `value` highlighted as the mention, as sent.
            `null` when the send omitted it (the whole `value` is highlighted) or the part
            carries no mention.
            *Characters are measured as UTF-16 code units. Most characters count as 1; some emoji count as 2.*

x-relay-websocket-close-codes:
  "1011": Relay could not load or commit delivery state; reconnect and resume.
  "1012": Relay is restarting; reconnect and resume.
  "4401": The Agent Token is invalid or revoked.
  "4408": The heartbeat timed out.
  "4410": Webhook delivery is now configured for this Agent.
````
